## app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/Engineering.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

import java.math.BigDecimal
import java.math.MathContext
import java.math.RoundingMode
import java.util.Locale
import kotlin.math.*

/**
 * Defines one scalar syntax so calculator inputs and module filters agree about explicit suffix
 * precedence. Construction holds metadata/helpers; physical validation is performed by the named
 * operations, not by field assignment.
 */
object Engineering {
    /** Accepted suffix exponents; case distinguishes milli from mega. */
    private val powers =
        mapOf(
            'p' to -12,
            'n' to -9,
            'u' to -6,
            'µ' to -6,
            'μ' to -6,
            'm' to -3,
            'k' to 3,
            'K' to 3,
            'M' to 6,
            'G' to 9,
            'T' to 12,
            'R' to 0,
            'r' to 0,
        )
    /** Allowed explicit physical units; unknown trailing text is rejected. */
    private val units = UnitCatalog.baseUnits
    /**
     * Anchored bare-number syntax checked before suffix parsing. Full-token anchoring rejects Java
     * f/d suffixes instead of treating them as valid scalar units.
     */
    private val plain = Regex("^[+-]?(?:[0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]*)?|\\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?$")
    /**
     * Numeric-head/suffix grammar permits embedded digits only for engineering notation. The suffix
     * is parsed separately; embedded digits are valid only for notation such as 4k7 or 2R2.
     */
    private val scalar =
        Regex("^([+-]?(?:[0-9]+(?:\\.[0-9]*)?|\\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?)(.*)$")

    /**
     * Retains explicit scale/unit metadata so a selector cannot multiply an already scaled value
     * twice.
     *
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @param explicitScale True when typed scale or units must override the dropdown multiplier.
     * @param unit Physical output unit; blank denotes a dimensionless result. Construction holds
     *   metadata/helpers; physical validation is performed by the named operations, not by field
     *   assignment.
     */
    data class Parsed(
        /** Input scalar in the operation’s documented units. */
        val value: Double,
        /**
         * True when the input already carries a unit/scale, preventing duplicate dropdown scaling.
         */
        val explicitScale: Boolean,
        /** Physical output unit; blank denotes a dimensionless result. */
        val unit: String = "",
    )

    /**
     * Distinguishes bare numbers from pasted physical values and preserves scale provenance for
     * dropdown precedence.
     *
     * @param text Input or output text as described above; treated as data, never executed.
     * @return A finite scalar plus scale/unit metadata, or null for unsupported syntax. Invalid
     *   input follows the nullable/typed-validation contract above; this operation performs no I/O.
     */
    fun parsed(text: String): Parsed? {
        // Accept both the Greek omega and the compatibility OHM SIGN in pasted values.
        val s =
            text
                .replace(Regex("(?i)meg"), "M")
                .trim()
                .replace('−', '-')
                .replace("Ω", "Ω")
                .replace(Regex("\\s+"), "")
        if (plain.matches(s))
            return s.toDoubleOrNull()?.takeIf(Double::isFinite)?.let { Parsed(it, false) }
        val match = scalar.matchEntire(s) ?: return null
        val number = match.groupValues[1]
        val tail = match.groupValues[2]
        if (tail.isEmpty()) return null
        if (tail in units && tail != "m")
            return number.toDoubleOrNull()?.takeIf(Double::isFinite)?.let { Parsed(it, true, tail) }
        val power = powers[tail[0]] ?: return null
        val rest = tail.drop(1)
        val digits = rest.takeWhile(Char::isDigit)
        val unit = rest.drop(digits.length)
        if (
            unit !in units ||
                (digits.isNotEmpty() && (number.contains('.') || number.contains('e', true)))
        )
            return null
        val significant = if (digits.isEmpty()) number else "$number.$digits"
        return significant
            .toDoubleOrNull()
            // Divide for negative scales so the reported 10 µF default matches the exact Double
            // literal 1e-5.
            ?.let { if (power < 0) it / 10.0.pow(-power) else it * 10.0.pow(power) }
            ?.takeIf(Double::isFinite)
            ?.let { Parsed(it, true, unit) }
    }

    /**
     * Accepts a finite scalar or returns null; explicit suffixes are applied only once.
     *
     * @param text Input or output text as described above; treated as data, never executed.
     * @return The finite base-unit scalar, or null for invalid or non-finite input. Invalid input
     *   follows the nullable/typed-validation contract above; this operation performs no I/O.
     */
    fun parse(text: String): Double? = parsed(text)?.value

    /**
     * Resolves explicit physical units before dropdown scale to prevent silent thousand-fold
     * errors.
     *
     * @param text Input or output text as described above; treated as data, never executed.
     * @param exponent Dropdown base-ten scale, ignored when text already supplies explicit scale.
     * @param fieldUnit Expected physical unit used to reject incompatible pasted values.
     * @return A finite scalar in the expected field unit, or null for incompatible units/invalid
     *   input. Invalid input follows the nullable/typed-validation contract above; this operation
     *   performs no I/O.
     */
    fun input(text: String, exponent: Int, fieldUnit: String = ""): Double? {
        // A bare m remains milli globally, but in a metre field its explicit physical unit wins.
        val compact = text.trim().replace(" ", "").replace('−', '-')
        val metres = if (fieldUnit == "m" && compact.endsWith("m")) compact.dropLast(1) else ""
        val quantity =
            if (plain.matches(metres))
                metres.toDoubleOrNull()?.takeIf(Double::isFinite)?.let { Parsed(it, true, "m") }
            else parsed(text)
        return quantity?.let {
            if (fieldUnit !in UnitCatalog.fieldUnits) return null
            val fieldScale = UnitCatalog.scale(fieldUnit)
            val baseUnit = UnitCatalog.canonical(fieldUnit)
            if (it.unit.isNotBlank() && baseUnit.isNotBlank() && it.unit != baseUnit) return null
            val normalised = if (it.unit.isNotBlank()) it.value / fieldScale else it.value
            (normalised * if (it.explicitScale) 1.0 else 10.0.pow(exponent)).takeIf(
                Double::isFinite
            )
        }
    }

    /**
     * Exposes suffix precedence to the UI without duplicating parser grammar.
     *
     * @param text Input or output text as described above; treated as data, never executed.
     * @param exponent Dropdown base-ten scale, ignored when text already supplies explicit scale.
     * @return True when explicit input scale overrides a non-base selector. Invalid input follows
     *   the nullable/typed-validation contract above; this operation performs no I/O.
     */
    fun ignoresSelector(text: String, exponent: Int): Boolean =
        exponent != 0 && parsed(text)?.explicitScale == true

    /**
     * Rounds human-readable decimals to four significant digits while retaining exact fractional
     * band tolerances.
     *
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @return Plain decimal text rounded to four significant digits, with trailing fractional zeros
     *   removed. Invalid physical constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator
     *   boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun decimal(value: Double): String {
        require(value.isFinite()) { Messages.INPUTS_EXCEED_THE_NUMERICAL_CALCULATION_RANGE }
        return BigDecimal.valueOf(if (value == 0.0) 0.0 else value)
            .round(MathContext(4, RoundingMode.HALF_UP))
            .stripTrailingZeros()
            .toPlainString()
    }

    /**
     * Uses ordinary decimal percentages so tolerance values never acquire milli-percent prefixes.
     *
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @return Rounded decimal text followed by the literal percent sign. Invalid physical
     *   constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no
     *   persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun percent(value: Double): String = decimal(value) + "%"

    /**
     * Separates physical engineering notation from unitless decimal/scientific notation to preserve
     * dimensional meaning.
     *
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @param unit Physical output unit; blank denotes a dimensionless result.
     * @return Formatted quantity text; dimensionless values never receive an SI prefix letter.
     *   Invalid physical constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to
     *   report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun format(value: Double, unit: String = ""): String {
        require(value.isFinite()) { Messages.INPUTS_EXCEED_THE_NUMERICAL_CALCULATION_RANGE }
        if (unit == "%") return percent(value)
        // Keep an already scaled label intact instead of emitting invalid compound prefixes.
        if (unit in UnitCatalog.plainDisplayUnits) return format(value) + " " + unit
        if (unit.isBlank() || unit == "V/V") {
            val rounded =
                BigDecimal.valueOf(if (value == 0.0) 0.0 else value)
                    .round(MathContext(6, RoundingMode.HALF_UP))
                    .stripTrailingZeros()
            val plain =
                if (value == 0.0 || abs(value) in 1e-4..1e6) rounded.toPlainString()
                else rounded.toString()
            return plain + if (unit.isBlank()) "" else " $unit"
        }
        if (value == 0.0) return "0 $unit".trim()
        var exponent = (floor(log10(abs(value)) / 3).toInt() * 3)
        if (exponent !in -12..12)
            return String.format(Locale.US, "%.6g", value) + if (unit.isBlank()) "" else " $unit"
        var scaled = value / 10.0.pow(exponent)
        // Promote a rounded mantissa at 1000 before choosing its prefix (avoid 1000 mΩ).
        if (abs(String.format(Locale.US, "%.6g", scaled).toDouble()) >= 1000.0 && exponent < 12) {
            exponent += 3
            scaled = value / 10.0.pow(exponent)
        }
        val prefix =
            mapOf(
                    -12 to "p",
                    -9 to "n",
                    -6 to "µ",
                    -3 to "m",
                    0 to "",
                    3 to "k",
                    6 to "M",
                    9 to "G",
                    12 to "T",
                )
                .getValue(exponent)
        val number =
            String.format(Locale.US, "%.6g", scaled).let {
                if ('.' in it && !it.contains('e', true)) it.trimEnd('0').trimEnd('.') else it
            }
        return "$number $prefix$unit".trim()
    }
}

/**
 * Keeps physical equations Android-independent so known physical points can be tested without a UI.
 * Construction holds metadata/helpers; physical validation is performed by the named operations,
 * not by field assignment.
 */
object Circuits {
    /**
     * Rejects non-positive and non-finite quantities before physical divisions and square roots.
     *
     * @param x Coordinate in this renderer’s documented canvas space.
     * @return Unit after all constraints pass. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun positive(vararg x: Double) {
        require(x.all { it.isFinite() && it > 0 }) { Messages.VALUES_MUST_BE_POSITIVE_AND_FINITE }
    }

    /**
     * Solves V=IR and P=VI from exactly two independent positive physical quantities.
     *
     * @param v Voltage in volts, or resistance scalar when used by the SMD encoder.
     * @param i Current in amperes.
     * @param r Resistance in ohms.
     * @param p Power in watts.
     * @return Voltage, current, resistance and power keyed by dimensional labels. Invalid physical
     *   constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no
     *   persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun ohm(v: Double?, i: Double?, r: Double?, p: Double?): Map<String, Double> {
        require(listOf(v, i, r, p).count { it != null } == 2) {
            Messages.ENTER_EXACTLY_TWO_OF_V_I_R_AND
        }
        positive(*listOfNotNull(v, i, r, p).toDoubleArray())
        val resistance =
            when {
                r != null -> r
                v != null && i != null -> v / i
                v != null && p != null -> v * v / p
                else -> p!! / (i!! * i)
            }
        val current =
            when {
                i != null -> i
                v != null -> v / resistance
                else -> sqrt(p!! / resistance)
            }
        return mapOf(
            Messages.VOLTAGE_V to current * resistance,
            Messages.CURRENT_A to current,
            Messages.RESISTANCE to resistance,
            Messages.POWER_W to current * current * resistance,
        )
    }

    /**
     * Includes the optional parallel load when evaluating the lower divider leg.
     *
     * @param v Voltage in volts, or resistance scalar when used by the SMD encoder.
     * @param r1 Upper/timing resistance in ohms.
     * @param r2 Lower/timing resistance in ohms.
     * @param load Optional parallel load resistance in ohms.
     * @return Output voltage in volts. Invalid physical constraints throw IllegalArgumentException
     *   for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun divider(v: Double, r1: Double, r2: Double, load: Double? = null): Double {
        positive(v, r1, r2)
        if (load != null) positive(load)
        val lower = if (load != null) parallel(listOf(r2, load)) else r2
        return v * lower / (r1 + lower)
    }

    /**
     * Adds positive component values; capacitor callers swap the series/parallel interpretation
     * explicitly.
     *
     * @param values Caller-owned field/component snapshot; not mutated by this operation.
     * @return Sum in the same physical units as the inputs. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun series(values: List<Double>): Double {
        require(values.isNotEmpty()) { Messages.ENTER_AT_LEAST_ONE_COMPONENT_VALUE }
        positive(*values.toDoubleArray())
        return values.sum()
    }

    /**
     * Uses reciprocal addition so a positive parallel resistance remains below either branch.
     *
     * @param values Caller-owned field/component snapshot; not mutated by this operation.
     * @return Reciprocal-sum equivalent in the input units. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun parallel(values: List<Double>): Double {
        series(values)
        return 1 / values.sumOf { 1 / it }
    }

    /**
     * Uses nominal NE555 one-third/two-thirds thresholds to calculate astable timing.
     *
     * @param r1 Upper/timing resistance in ohms.
     * @param r2 Lower/timing resistance in ohms.
     * @param c Capacitance in farads.
     * @return Frequency in Hz, duty in percent and high/low durations in seconds. Invalid physical
     *   constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no
     *   persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun astable(r1: Double, r2: Double, c: Double): Map<String, Double> {
        positive(r1, r2, c)
        val h = ln(2.0) * (r1 + r2) * c
        val l = ln(2.0) * r2 * c
        return mapOf(
            Messages.FREQUENCY_HZ to 1 / (h + l),
            Messages.DUTY to 100 * h / (h + l),
            Messages.HIGH_S to h,
            Messages.LOW_S to l,
        )
    }

    /**
     * Uses the nominal NE555 two-thirds-supply threshold for monostable pulse duration.
     *
     * @param r Resistance in ohms.
     * @param c Capacitance in farads.
     * @return Nominal pulse duration in seconds. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun mono(r: Double, c: Double): Double {
        positive(r, c)
        return ln(3.0) * r * c
    }

    /**
     * Finds a limiting resistor per LED string; parallel strings require separate limiting
     * resistors.
     *
     * @param v Voltage in volts, or resistance scalar when used by the SMD encoder.
     * @param vf Forward voltage drop of one LED, in volts.
     * @param i Current in amperes.
     * @param n Preferred-series size or LED count as stated by this operation.
     * @return Per-string limiting resistance in ohms. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun led(v: Double, vf: Double, i: Double, n: Double = 1.0): Double {
        positive(v, vf, i, n)
        require(v > vf * n) { Messages.SUPPLY_MUST_EXCEED_THE_LED_STRING_VOLTAGE }
        return (v - vf * n) / i
    }

    /**
     * Includes adjust-pin current so high divider resistances do not silently omit its voltage
     * contribution.
     *
     * @param r1 Upper/timing resistance in ohms.
     * @param r2 Lower/timing resistance in ohms.
     * @param iadj Regulator adjust-pin current in amperes.
     * @return Nominal regulated output voltage in volts. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun lm317(r1: Double, r2: Double, iadj: Double = 50e-6): Double {
        positive(r1, r2)
        require(iadj.isFinite() && iadj >= 0) { Messages.ADJUST_CURRENT_MUST_BE_ZERO_OR_POSITIVE }
        return 1.25 * (1 + r2 / r1) + iadj * r2
    }

    /**
     * Computes the ideal first-order cutoff rather than implying a component-specific bandwidth
     * guarantee.
     *
     * @param r Resistance in ohms.
     * @param c Capacitance in farads.
     * @return Ideal cutoff frequency in hertz. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun rc(r: Double, c: Double): Double {
        positive(r, c)
        return 1 / (2 * PI * r * c)
    }

    /**
     * Inverts the empirical IPC-2221 current equation; the result is an estimate, not certified
     * ampacity.
     *
     * @param i Current in amperes.
     * @param dt Permitted temperature rise in degrees Celsius.
     * @param oz Copper weight in ounces per square foot.
     * @param internal True selects the IPC internal-layer coefficient.
     * @return Estimated width in millimetres. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun traceWidth(i: Double, dt: Double, oz: Double, internal: Boolean): Double {
        positive(i, dt, oz)
        // IPC-2221 uses square mils: I=k ΔT^0.44 A^0.725; internal layers use half the external k.
        val k = if (internal) 0.024 else 0.048
        val area = (i / (k * dt.pow(0.44))).pow(1 / 0.725) // square mils
        return area / (oz * 1.378) * 0.0254 // mil to mm; nominal 35 µm per oz
    }

    /**
     * Includes both conductors of a DC loop while accepting one-way cable length.
     *
     * @param length One-way conductor length in metres.
     * @param area Conductor cross-section in square millimetres.
     * @param i Current in amperes.
     * @param rho Resistivity in ohm square millimetres per metre.
     * @return DC two-wire loop drop in volts. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun voltageDrop(length: Double, area: Double, i: Double, rho: Double = 0.017241): Double {
        positive(length, area, i, rho)
        return 2 * length * rho * i / area
    }

    /**
     * Evaluates the nominal platinum curve over the supported temperature interval, with an
     * optional linear approximation.
     *
     * @param t Temperature in degrees Celsius.
     * @param r0 Nominal RTD resistance at zero degrees Celsius in ohms.
     * @param linear True selects the stated linear platinum approximation.
     * @return Nominal resistance in ohms. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun rtd(t: Double, r0: Double, linear: Boolean = false): Double {
        require(t in -200.0..850.0) { Messages.TEMPERATURE_MUST_BE_BETWEEN_200_AND_850_C }
        positive(r0)
        // Platinum CVD: A=3.9083e−3, B=−5.775e−7, C=−4.183e−12; the cubic correction is below zero
        // only.
        // Linear mode deliberately uses alpha=0.00385 and is not the full CVD curve.
        return if (linear) r0 * (1 + 0.00385 * t)
        else
            r0 *
                (1 + 3.9083e-3 * t - 5.775e-7 * t * t +
                    if (t < 0) -4.183e-12 * (t - 100) * t * t * t else 0.0)
    }

    /**
     * Inverts the monotonic platinum curve and quantises microdegrees to remove bisection residue
     * near zero.
     *
     * @param r Resistance in ohms.
     * @param r0 Nominal RTD resistance at zero degrees Celsius in ohms.
     * @param linear True selects the stated linear platinum approximation.
     * @return Temperature quantised to 1e-6 °C, with signed zero normalised. Invalid physical
     *   constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no
     *   persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun rtdTemperature(r: Double, r0: Double, linear: Boolean = false): Double {
        positive(r, r0)
        if (linear)
            return ((r / r0 - 1) / 0.00385).also {
                require(it in -200.0..850.0) {
                    Messages.RESISTANCE_CORRESPONDS_TO_A_TEMPERATURE_OUTSIDE_200_850
                }
            }
        require(r in rtd(-200.0, r0)..rtd(850.0, r0)) { Messages.RESISTANCE_OUTSIDE_200_850_C }
        var lo = -200.0
        var hi = 850.0
        repeat(70) {
            val m = (lo + hi) / 2
            if (rtd(m, r0) < r) lo = m else hi = m
        }
        return (round(((lo + hi) / 2) * 1e6) / 1e6).let { if (it == 0.0) 0.0 else it }
    }
}

/**
 * Shares colour, preferred-value and printed-marking rules across forward and reverse component
 * lookups. Construction holds metadata/helpers; physical validation is performed by the named
 * operations, not by field assignment.
 */
object Resistors {
    /** Colour names in standard band-index order. */
    val names =
        listOf(
            Messages.BLACK,
            Messages.BROWN,
            Messages.RED,
            Messages.ORANGE,
            Messages.YELLOW,
            Messages.GREEN,
            Messages.BLUE,
            Messages.VIOLET,
            Messages.GREY,
            Messages.WHITE,
            Messages.GOLD,
            Messages.SILVER,
        )
    /** Tolerance percentages keyed by colour; these numbers are percent, not fractions. */
    val tolerance =
        mapOf(1 to 1.0, 2 to 2.0, 5 to 0.5, 6 to 0.25, 7 to 0.1, 8 to 0.05, 10 to 5.0, 11 to 10.0)

    /**
     * Converts significant colour digits and a decimal multiplier into a physical resistance.
     *
     * @param digits Significant colour-band digit indices.
     * @param multiplier Base-ten exponent, including negative gold/silver multipliers.
     * @return Decoded physical resistance in ohms, or a preference snapshot in the persistence
     *   codec. Invalid physical constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator
     *   boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun decode(digits: List<Int>, multiplier: Int): Double {
        require(digits.size in 2..3 && digits[0] in 1..9 && digits.all { it in 0..9 }) {
            Messages.SELECT_TWO_OR_THREE_VALID_DIGITS_WITH_A
        }
        require(multiplier in -2..9) { Messages.MULTIPLIER_MUST_BE_BETWEEN_0_01_AND_ONE }
        return digits.fold(0) { a, b -> a * 10 + b } * 10.0.pow(multiplier)
    }

    /**
     * Rounds resistance to the representable band precision; the persistence codec instead
     * serialises its state argument.
     *
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @param five True uses three significant digits (five-band resistor).
     * @return Band digits and multiplier exponent, or JSON text in the persistence codec. Invalid
     *   physical constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report;
     *   no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun encode(value: Double, five: Boolean = false): List<Int> {
        Circuits.positive(value)
        val count = if (five) 3 else 2
        var e = floor(log10(value)).toInt() - count + 1
        var d = (value / 10.0.pow(e)).roundToInt()
        if (d >= 10.0.pow(count)) {
            d /= 10
            e++
        }
        require(e in -2..9) { Messages.VALUE_OUTSIDE_AVAILABLE_BAND_RANGE }
        return d.toString().map { it.digitToInt() } + e
    }

    /** Preferred E12 mantissas for a normalised decade. */
    val e12 = listOf(1.0, 1.2, 1.5, 1.8, 2.2, 2.7, 3.3, 3.9, 4.7, 5.6, 6.8, 8.2)
    /** Preferred E24 mantissas for a normalised decade. */
    val e24 =
        listOf(
            1.0,
            1.1,
            1.2,
            1.3,
            1.5,
            1.6,
            1.8,
            2.0,
            2.2,
            2.4,
            2.7,
            3.0,
            3.3,
            3.6,
            3.9,
            4.3,
            4.7,
            5.1,
            5.6,
            6.2,
            6.8,
            7.5,
            8.2,
            9.1,
        )
    /** Preferred E96 integer significands; normalisation divides by 100. */
    val e96 =
        listOf(
            100,
            102,
            105,
            107,
            110,
            113,
            115,
            118,
            121,
            124,
            127,
            130,
            133,
            137,
            140,
            143,
            147,
            150,
            154,
            158,
            162,
            165,
            169,
            174,
            178,
            182,
            187,
            191,
            196,
            200,
            205,
            210,
            215,
            221,
            226,
            232,
            237,
            243,
            249,
            255,
            261,
            267,
            274,
            280,
            287,
            294,
            301,
            309,
            316,
            324,
            332,
            340,
            348,
            357,
            365,
            374,
            383,
            392,
            402,
            412,
            422,
            432,
            442,
            453,
            464,
            475,
            487,
            499,
            511,
            523,
            536,
            549,
            562,
            576,
            590,
            604,
            619,
            634,
            649,
            665,
            681,
            698,
            715,
            732,
            750,
            768,
            787,
            806,
            825,
            845,
            866,
            887,
            909,
            931,
            953,
            976,
        )

    /**
     * Keeps preferred mantissas independent of decade expansion for nearest-value and ratio
     * searches.
     *
     * @param n Preferred-series size or LED count as stated by this operation.
     * @return Normalised preferred mantissas for the requested series. Invalid input follows the
     *   nullable/typed-validation contract above; this operation performs no I/O.
     */
    fun standard(n: Int) =
        when (n) {
            12 -> e12
            24 -> e24
            else -> e96.map { it / 100.0 }
        }

    /**
     * Searches adjacent decades so candidates near a decade boundary are not missed.
     *
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @param n Preferred-series size or LED count as stated by this operation.
     * @param up True restricts nearest-value candidates to at least the requested value.
     * @return Closest permitted standard resistance in ohms. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun nearest(value: Double, n: Int = 24, up: Boolean = false): Double {
        Circuits.positive(value)
        val e = floor(log10(value)).toInt()
        return ((e - 1)..(e + 1))
            .flatMap { power -> standard(n).map { it * 10.0.pow(power) } }
            .filter { !up || it >= value }
            .minBy { abs(it - value) }
    }

    /**
     * Decodes numeric, R-decimal and EIA-96 markings while rejecting arbitrary trailing text.
     *
     * @param code Printed component marking, interpreted as data.
     * @return Decoded resistance in ohms. Invalid physical constraints throw
     *   IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun smd(code: String): Double {
        val s = code.uppercase().trim()
        if (s.contains('R') && !(s.length == 3 && s.last() == 'R' && s.take(2).all(Char::isDigit)))
            return Engineering.parse(s) ?: throw IllegalArgumentException(Messages.INVALID_R_NOTATION)
        if (s.length == 3 && s.take(2).all(Char::isDigit) && s.last().isLetter()) {
            val idx = s.take(2).toInt()
            require(idx in 1..96) { Messages.EIA_96_CODE_MUST_START_WITH_A_NUMBER }
            val m =
                mapOf(
                    'Z' to 0.001,
                    'Y' to 0.01,
                    'R' to 0.01,
                    'X' to 0.1,
                    'S' to 0.1,
                    'A' to 1.0,
                    'B' to 10.0,
                    'H' to 10.0,
                    'C' to 100.0,
                    'D' to 1000.0,
                    'E' to 10000.0,
                    'F' to 100000.0,
                )[s.last()] ?: throw IllegalArgumentException(Messages.INVALID_EIA_96_MULTIPLIER)
            return e96[idx - 1] * m
        }
        require(s.length in 3..4 && s.all(Char::isDigit)) {
            Messages.USE_3_4_DIGITS_R_NOTATION_OR_EIA
        }
        return s.dropLast(1).toDouble() * 10.0.pow(s.last().digitToInt())
    }

    /**
     * Reports printed-code approximations and plain-decimal R notation without embedding scientific
     * exponents in markings.
     *
     * @param v Voltage in volts, or resistance scalar when used by the SMD encoder.
     * @return Printed-code approximations and R notation, or an explicit practical-range message.
     *   Invalid physical constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to
     *   report; no persistence occurs here.
     */
    fun smdCodes(v: Double): String {
        Circuits.positive(v)
        /**
         * Uses numeric significant digits when representable and falls back to plain R notation
         * otherwise.
         *
         * @param d Number of significant digits in a printed numeric marking.
         * @return One numeric marking or a plain-decimal R-notation alternative. Invalid physical
         *   constraints throw IllegalArgumentException for the calculator boundary to report; no
         *   persistence occurs here.
         */
        fun numeric(d: Int): String {
            val e = floor(log10(v)).toInt() - d + 1
            val sig = (v / 10.0.pow(e)).roundToInt()
            return if (e in 0..9 && sig < 10.0.pow(d))
                "$sig$e (${Engineering.format(sig*10.0.pow(e),"Ω")})"
            else {
                val plain = BigDecimal.valueOf(v).stripTrailingZeros().toPlainString()
                val notation = if ('.' in plain) plain.replace('.', 'R') else plain + "R0"
                if (notation.length <= 24) Messages.rNotation(notation)
                else Messages.NO_PRACTICAL_PRINTED_R_NOTATION_EXISTS_FOR_THIS
            }
        }
        val candidates =
            (-3..5).flatMap { e ->
                e96.mapIndexed { ix, x ->
                    Triple(
                        abs(x * 10.0.pow(e) - v),
                        "%02d".format(ix + 1) +
                            mapOf(
                                -3 to "Z",
                                -2 to "Y",
                                -1 to "X",
                                0 to "A",
                                1 to "B",
                                2 to "C",
                                3 to "D",
                                4 to "E",
                                5 to "F",
                            )[e],
                        x * 10.0.pow(e),
                    )
                }
            }
        val best = candidates.minBy { it.first }
        return Messages.smdResult(
            numeric(2),
            numeric(3),
            best.second,
            Engineering.format(best.third, "Ω"),
        )
    }
}
````

## app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/EngineeringSearch.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

import com.electrokit.app.data.FaultCode

/** Pure filter logic is shared with tests; browsing never rewrites source fault fields. */
object EngineeringSearch {
    /**
     * Combines all selected local fault filters without changing dataset order.
     *
     * @param all Complete source list.
     * @param query Code/message query, trimmed and matched case-insensitively.
     * @param group Exact group or blank for All.
     * @param reset Exact supplied reset type or blank for All.
     * @param system Derived browsing index or blank for All; not a certified location.
     * @param bookmarks Null disables this filter; otherwise only these exact code strings match.
     * @return Stable-order matching rows; empty lists are valid and no errors are thrown.
     */
    fun faults(
        all: List<FaultCode>,
        query: String,
        group: String = "",
        reset: String = "",
        system: String = "",
        bookmarks: Set<String>? = null,
    ): List<FaultCode> =
        all.filter {
            (query.isBlank() ||
                it.code.contains(query.trim(), true) ||
                it.message.contains(query.trim(), true)) &&
                (group.isBlank() || it.group == group) &&
                (reset.isBlank() || it.reset == reset) &&
                (system.isBlank() || it.system == system) &&
                (bookmarks == null || it.code in bookmarks)
        }
}
````

## app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/EngineeringTools.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

import kotlin.math.*

/**
 * User-visible validation messages for the new pure calculator boundary; no UI resources or I/O.
 */
object EngineeringMessages {
    /** Missing/nonfinite/wrong-dimension scalar feedback. */
    const val INPUT = "Enter a finite value in every required field, using the displayed units."
    /** Invalid physical range feedback. */
    const val RANGE =
        "Check the physical ranges: positive quantities, PF/efficiency limits and whole-number poles or teeth."
    /** Overflow/underflow feedback. */
    const val NUMERICAL =
        "The values exceed the supported numerical range; use less extreme inputs."
}

/** Pure motor, power, geometry and kinematic calculations with explicit physical assumptions. */
object EngineeringTools {
    /** Exact source/target units and numerical factors for the available converter choices. */
    val conversions =
        linkedMapOf(
            "W → kW" to Triple("W", "kW", .001),
            "kW → W" to Triple("kW", "W", 1000.0),
            "A → mA" to Triple("A", "mA", 1000.0),
            "mA → A" to Triple("mA", "A", .001),
            "mm → m" to Triple("mm", "m", .001),
            "m → mm" to Triple("m", "mm", 1000.0),
            "m/s → km/h" to Triple("m/s", "km/h", 3.6),
            "km/h → m/s" to Triple("km/h", "m/s", 1 / 3.6),
            "kWh → J" to Triple("kWh", "J", 3600000.0),
            "J → kWh" to Triple("J", "kWh", 1 / 3600000.0),
        )

    /**
     * Evaluates an explicit tool input map; no missing physical parameter is defaulted.
     *
     * @param id Stable calculator ID from engineering_tools.json.
     * @param values Raw saved text with optional unit suffixes and conversion selection.
     * @return Value with substitution steps, or actionable Error for invalid input; no input
     *   exception escapes.
     */
    fun calculate(id: String, values: Map<String, String>): Calculation {
        return try {
            /**
             * Resolves one required finite scalar in its declared field unit.
             *
             * @param key Stable field key.
             * @param unit Expected unit; blank is explicitly dimensionless.
             * @return Valid scalar or throws IllegalArgumentException, caught by the boundary.
             */
            fun x(key: String, unit: String = ""): Double {
                val raw = values[key].orEmpty()
                // The legacy parser allows omitted dimensions; new explicit ratio fields do not.
                if (unit.isBlank() && !Engineering.parsed(raw)?.unit.isNullOrBlank())
                    throw IllegalArgumentException(EngineeringMessages.INPUT)
                return Engineering.input(raw, 0, unit)
                    ?: throw IllegalArgumentException(EngineeringMessages.INPUT)
            }
            /**
             * Checks a positive physical quantity without conflating zero with missing input.
             *
             * @param v Parsed physical value.
             * @return Valid positive value; invalid values throw the range message, caught above.
             */
            fun positive(v: Double): Double {
                require(v > 0) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                return v
            }
            /**
             * Formats finite outputs without silently printing Infinity, NaN or negative zero.
             *
             * @param v Calculated scalar.
             * @param unit Display unit; blank denotes a dimensionless result.
             * @return Six-significant-digit text; nonfinite results throw and become a numerical
             *   error.
             */
            fun f(v: Double, unit: String = ""): String {
                require(v.isFinite()) { EngineeringMessages.NUMERICAL }
                if (unit == "%") return Engineering.percent(v)
                return Engineering.format(if (v == 0.0) 0.0 else v) +
                    if (unit.isBlank()) "" else " $unit"
            }
            val text =
                when (id) {
                    // Balanced sinusoidal apparent, active and fundamental reactive power, SI
                    // inputs.
                    "single-phase",
                    "three-phase" -> {
                        val v = positive(x("v", "V"))
                        val i = positive(x("i", "A"))
                        val pf = x("pf")
                        require(pf in 0.0..1.0) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                        val factor = if (id == "three-phase") sqrt(3.0) else 1.0
                        val s = factor * v * i
                        "S = ${f(factor)} × ${f(v)} × ${f(i)} = ${f(s / 1000, "kVA")}\nP = S × ${f(pf)} = ${f(s * pf / 1000, "kW")}\nQ = S × √(1 − PF²) = ${f(s * sqrt(1 - pf * pf) / 1000, "kVAR")}"
                    }
                    // Shaft kW is converted to W before dividing by balanced input voltage and
                    // efficiency.
                    "motor-current" -> {
                        val p = positive(x("p", "kW"))
                        val v = positive(x("v", "V"))
                        val pf = x("pf")
                        val eta = x("eta", "%")
                        require(pf > 0 && pf <= 1 && eta > 0 && eta <= 100) {
                            EngineeringMessages.RANGE
                        }
                        "I = ${f(p)} × 1000 / (√3 × ${f(v)} × ${f(pf)} × ${f(eta / 100)})\nCurrent: ${f(p * 1000 / (sqrt(3.0) * v * pf * (eta / 100)), "A")}"
                    }
                    "efficiency" -> {
                        val out = positive(x("out", "kW"))
                        val input = positive(x("in", "kW"))
                        require(out <= input) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                        "η = 100 × ${f(out)} / ${f(input)}\nEfficiency: ${f(100 * out / input, "%")}"
                    }
                    "power-factor" -> {
                        val p = x("p", "kW")
                        val s = positive(x("s", "kVA"))
                        require(p >= 0 && p <= s) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                        "PF = ${f(p)} / ${f(s)}\nPower factor: ${f(p / s)}"
                    }
                    // T in N·m from shaft W and rpm, using the exact 60/(2π) relationship.
                    "torque" -> {
                        val p = positive(x("p", "kW"))
                        val n = positive(x("n", "rpm"))
                        "T = 60 × ${f(p)} × 1000 / (2π × ${f(n)})\nTorque: ${f(60 * p * 1000 / (2 * PI * n), "N·m")}"
                    }
                    // Pole count is an explicit positive even integer; no 6-pole inference is
                    // hidden.
                    "slip",
                    "frequency-speed" -> {
                        val freq = positive(x("f", "Hz"))
                        val poles = positive(x("poles"))
                        require(poles >= 2 && poles % 2 == 0.0 && poles <= 1000) {
                            EngineeringMessages.RANGE
                        }
                        val ns = 120 * freq / poles
                        if (id == "slip") {
                            val n = x("n", "rpm")
                            // Negative slip represents regeneration above synchronous speed.
                            require(n >= 0) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                            "ns = 120 × ${f(freq)} / ${f(poles)} = ${f(ns, "rpm")}\ns = 100 × (${f(ns)} − ${f(n)}) / ${f(ns)}\nSlip: ${f(100 * (ns - n) / ns, "%")}"
                        } else {
                            val slip = x("slip", "%")
                            require(slip < 100) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                            "ns = 120 × ${f(freq)} / ${f(poles)} = ${f(ns, "rpm")}\nn = ${f(ns)} × (1 − ${f(slip)} / 100)\nRotor speed: ${f(ns * (1 - slip / 100), "rpm")}"
                        }
                    }
                    // Ideal persons/hour from metres/second, actual step pitch and explicit
                    // occupancy.
                    "capacity" -> {
                        val v = positive(x("v", "m/s"))
                        val pitch = positive(x("pitch", "m"))
                        val occ = x("occupancy")
                        require(occ >= 0) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                        "C = 3600 × ${f(v)} × ${f(occ)} / ${f(pitch)}\nTheoretical capacity: ${f(3600 * v * occ / pitch, "persons/h")}"
                    }
                    "gear-ratio" -> {
                        val input = positive(x("input", "rpm"))
                        val output = positive(x("output", "rpm"))
                        "ratio = ${f(input)} / ${f(output)}\nReduction ratio: ${f(input / output)}"
                    }
                    "gear" -> {
                        val n = positive(x("n", "rpm"))
                        val ratio = positive(x("ratio"))
                        "nout = ${f(n)} / ${f(ratio)}\nOutput speed: ${f(n / ratio, "rpm")}"
                    }
                    // Pitch-line chain speed; all geometry and total drive reduction are entered
                    // explicitly.
                    "step-speed" -> {
                        val n = positive(x("n", "rpm"))
                        val ratio = positive(x("ratio"))
                        val teeth = positive(x("teeth"))
                        val pitch = positive(x("pitch", "m"))
                        require(teeth % 1 == 0.0) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                        "v = (${f(n)} / ${f(ratio)}) × ${f(teeth)} × ${f(pitch)} / 60\nStep-chain speed: ${f(n / ratio * teeth * pitch / 60, "m/s")}"
                    }
                    "energy" -> {
                        val p = x("p", "kW")
                        val h = x("h", "h")
                        require(p >= 0 && h >= 0) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                        "E = ${f(p)} × ${f(h)}\nElectrical energy: ${f(p * h, "kWh")}"
                    }
                    "geometry" -> {
                        val length = positive(x("length", "m"))
                        val degrees = x("angle", "°")
                        require(degrees > 0 && degrees < 90) { EngineeringMessages.RANGE }
                        val angle = degrees * PI / 180
                        "H = ${f(length)} × sin(${f(degrees)}°) = ${f(length * sin(angle), "m")}\nProjection = ${f(length)} × cos(${f(degrees)}°) = ${f(length * cos(angle), "m")}"
                    }
                    "unit-converter" -> {
                        val pair =
                            conversions[values["conversion"]]
                                ?: throw IllegalArgumentException(EngineeringMessages.INPUT)
                        val value = x("x", pair.first)
                        "${f(value, pair.first)} × ${f(pair.third)}\nConverted value: ${f(value * pair.third, pair.second)}"
                    }
                    else -> throw IllegalArgumentException(EngineeringMessages.INPUT)
                }
            Calculation.Value(text)
        } catch (failure: IllegalArgumentException) {
            Calculation.Error(
                failure.message?.takeIf {
                    it in
                        listOf(
                            EngineeringMessages.INPUT,
                            EngineeringMessages.RANGE,
                            EngineeringMessages.NUMERICAL,
                        )
                } ?: EngineeringMessages.NUMERICAL
            )
        } catch (cancelled: java.util.concurrent.CancellationException) {
            throw cancelled
        } catch (_: Exception) {
            Calculation.Error(EngineeringMessages.NUMERICAL)
        }
    }
}
````

## app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/LocalPin.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

import java.security.MessageDigest
import javax.crypto.SecretKeyFactory
import javax.crypto.spec.PBEKeySpec

/** Verifies the initial local access code without storing its clear text in UI or preferences.
 * Uses Android API-24-compatible PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA1. This three-digit offline restriction cannot resist APK analysis or exhaustive guessing.
 */
object LocalPin {
    /** Salted PBKDF2 verification record for the initial local code; never a strong secret. */
    private val expected = "001a6f2e2dfa22673ef59adb2db54bb8c7f4aeeb9736118f6047c43c3e188bef"
        .chunked(2).map { it.toInt(16).toByte() }.toByteArray()

    /** Derives and compares a candidate; invalid lengths never reach the expensive KDF.
 * @param candidate Untrusted code string; only three ASCII digits are eligible.
 * @return True only when the constant-time derived-key comparison succeeds.
 */
    fun verify(candidate: String): Boolean {
        if (!candidate.matches(Regex("[0-9]{3}"))) return false
        val spec = PBEKeySpec(candidate.toCharArray(), "ELECTRO-local-access-v1".toByteArray(), 120000, 256)
        return try {
            MessageDigest.isEqual(expected, SecretKeyFactory.getInstance("PBKDF2WithHmacSHA1").generateSecret(spec).encoded)
        } finally { spec.clearPassword() }
    }
}
````

## app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/NumericFilter.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

/**
 * Keeps numeric filtering separate from text search and component prose. Construction holds
 * metadata/helpers; physical validation is performed by the named operations, not by field
 * assignment.
 */
object NumericFilter {
    /**
     * Separates invalid numeric bounds from a legitimate empty result set.
     *
     * @param minimum Optional lower numeric bound.
     * @param maximum Optional upper numeric bound.
     * @return Null for valid bounds, otherwise actionable validation prose. Invalid input follows
     *   the nullable/typed-validation contract above; this operation performs no I/O.
     */
    fun validation(minimum: String, maximum: String): String? {
        val min = Engineering.parse(minimum)
        val max = Engineering.parse(maximum)
        return when {
            minimum.isNotBlank() && min == null -> Messages.ENTER_A_VALID_MINIMUM_VALUE
            maximum.isNotBlank() && max == null -> Messages.ENTER_A_VALID_MAXIMUM_VALUE
            min != null && max != null && min > max -> Messages.MINIMUM_MUST_NOT_EXCEED_MAXIMUM
            else -> null
        }
    }

    /**
     * Applies explicit numeric bounds only to parseable metadata; invalid filters never match
     * accidentally.
     *
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @param minimum Optional lower numeric bound.
     * @param maximum Optional upper numeric bound.
     * @return True only when the scalar meets both valid optional bounds. Invalid input follows the
     *   nullable/typed-validation contract above; this operation performs no I/O.
     */
    fun matches(value: String?, minimum: String, maximum: String): Boolean {
        if (validation(minimum, maximum) != null) return false
        val number = Engineering.parse(value.orEmpty()) ?: return false
        return (minimum.isBlank() || number >= Engineering.parse(minimum)!!) &&
            (maximum.isBlank() || number <= Engineering.parse(maximum)!!)
    }
}
````

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

/**
 * Shares declared physical-unit rules between field validation and pasted-scalar parsing; no I/O.
 */
object UnitCatalog {
    /**
     * Base units retain field-specific conventions such as millimetres and ounces per square foot.
     */
    val baseUnits =
        setOf(
            "",
            "Ω",
            "F",
            "H",
            "V",
            "A",
            "Hz",
            "s",
            "W",
            "mm",
            "mm²",
            "%",
            "°C",
            "mAh",
            "KiB",
            "bytes",
            "m",
            "m/s",
            "oz/ft²",
            "°C/W",
            "VA",
            "var",
            "rpm",
            "h",
            "kWh",
            "J",
            "°",
            "km/h",
        )
    /** Already-scaled or non-SI units must not acquire another prefix, such as mmm or mmA. */
    val plainDisplayUnits =
        setOf("mm", "mm²", "mA", "kW", "mAh", "KiB", "bytes", "°C", "°C/W", "oz/ft²")
    /** Non-base field units convert through their canonical physical unit exactly once. */
    private val aliases =
        mapOf("mA" to ("A" to 0.001), "kW" to ("W" to 1000.0), "kVA" to ("VA" to 1000.0))
    /**
     * Accepted field units are derived from parser units, preventing separate lists from drifting.
     */
    val fieldUnits = baseUnits + aliases.keys

    /**
     * Resolves a field alias before comparing pasted physical dimensions.
     *
     * @param unit Declared field unit.
     * @return Canonical unit; unknown units remain unchanged for validation to reject. No
     *   exceptions.
     */
    fun canonical(unit: String): String = aliases[unit]?.first ?: unit

    /**
     * Provides the conversion from a declared field quantity to its canonical unit.
     *
     * @param unit Declared field unit.
     * @return Scale factor; base units use one. No I/O or validation exceptions.
     */
    fun scale(unit: String): Double = aliases[unit]?.second ?: 1.0
}
````

## app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/UnitConversions.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

/** Named linear unit groups use exact SI scale factors; temperature has explicit affine offsets. */
object UnitConversions {
    /** Canonical scale to each group's SI base unit, without mixing physical dimensions. */
    val groups = linkedMapOf(
        "Voltage" to linkedMapOf("V" to 1.0, "mV" to 1e-3, "kV" to 1e3),
        "Current" to linkedMapOf("A" to 1.0, "mA" to 1e-3, "µA" to 1e-6),
        "Power" to linkedMapOf("W" to 1.0, "kW" to 1e3, "MW" to 1e6),
        "Resistance" to linkedMapOf("Ω" to 1.0, "kΩ" to 1e3, "MΩ" to 1e6),
        "Capacitance" to linkedMapOf("F" to 1.0, "µF" to 1e-6, "nF" to 1e-9, "pF" to 1e-12),
        "Frequency" to linkedMapOf("Hz" to 1.0, "kHz" to 1e3, "MHz" to 1e6),
        "Length" to linkedMapOf("m" to 1.0, "mm" to 1e-3, "cm" to 1e-2, "in" to 0.0254, "ft" to 0.3048),
        "Temperature" to linkedMapOf("°C" to 1.0, "°F" to 1.0, "K" to 1.0)
    )

    /** Converts within one dimension, with the selected unit owning the scale exactly once.
     * @param group Named physical dimension.
     * @param from Explicit source unit.
     * @param to Explicit destination unit.
     * @param value Finite scalar in the source unit; suffix scaling belongs outside this API.
     * @return Converted scalar, rejecting mismatched units, overflow and temperatures below absolute zero.
     */
    fun convert(group: String, from: String, to: String, value: Double): Double {
        require(value.isFinite()) { "Enter a finite decimal value." }
        val units = requireNotNull(groups[group]) { "Unknown unit group." }
        require(from in units && to in units) { "Choose units from the same physical dimension." }
        val result = if (group == "Temperature") {
            val kelvin = when(from) { "°C" -> value + 273.15; "°F" -> (value - 32) * 5 / 9 + 273.15; else -> value }
            require(kelvin >= -1e-10) { "Temperature is below absolute zero." }
            when(to) { "°C" -> kelvin.coerceAtLeast(0.0) - 273.15; "°F" -> (kelvin.coerceAtLeast(0.0) - 273.15) * 9 / 5 + 32; else -> kelvin.coerceAtLeast(0.0) }
        } else value * units.getValue(from) / units.getValue(to)
        require(result.isFinite()) { "Conversion exceeds the numerical range." }
        return result
    }
}
````

## app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/WorkbenchTools.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

import kotlin.math.*

/** SI-input engineering utility metadata.
 * @property id Stable route key.
 * @property title Display name.
 * @property fields Named input labels and explicit units.
 * @property formula Physical model used to derive the result.
 * @property limitation Boundary of the simplified calculation.
 */
data class WorkbenchTool(val id: String, val title: String, val fields: List<String>, val formula: String, val limitation: String)

/** Additional tools use explicit assumptions instead of embedding cable or equipment ratings. */
object WorkbenchTools {
    /** Public utility catalogue, independent of protected controller reference data. */
    val all = listOf(
        WorkbenchTool("transformer", "Ideal transformer", listOf("Primary voltage (V)", "Primary turns", "Secondary turns"), "Vs = Vp × Ns / Np", "Ideal AC transformer ratio only; losses, insulation, frequency, VA and regulation are not modeled."),
        WorkbenchTool("ups", "Battery / UPS runtime", listOf("Battery voltage (V)", "Capacity (Ah)", "Usable depth (%)", "Efficiency (%)", "Load (W)"), "t = V × Ah × depth/100 × efficiency/100 / P", "Constant-power estimate. Battery aging, temperature, discharge-rate effects and inverter standby losses are excluded. Not a runtime guarantee."),
        WorkbenchTool("cable", "DC cable voltage-drop sizing", listOf("One-way length (m)", "Current (A)", "Resistivity (Ω·mm²/m)", "Allowed drop (V)"), "A = 2 × ρ × L × I / ΔV", "Two-conductor DC resistance model with user-entered resistivity. This does not select code-compliant cable, insulation, ampacity, protection, temperature or standard sizes."),
        WorkbenchTool("pf", "Single-phase power factor", listOf("Real power (W)", "RMS voltage (V)", "RMS current (A)"), "PF = P / (Vrms × Irms)", "Single-phase total power factor. This does not resolve leading/lagging behavior, harmonics or three-phase imbalance."),
        WorkbenchTool("energy", "Energy consumption", listOf("Power (W)", "Time (h)", "Price per kWh"), "E = P × t / 1000; cost = E × price", "Constant power and a flat user-entered tariff; demand charges and time-of-use rates are excluded."),
        WorkbenchTool("temperature", "Temperature converter", listOf("Celsius (°C)"), "°F = °C × 9/5 + 32; K = °C + 273.15", "Thermodynamic temperature cannot be below absolute zero."),
        WorkbenchTool("scientific", "Scientific calculator", listOf("Expression"), "+ − * / ^ ( ) sqrt(x) sin(x) cos(x) tan(x) ln(x) log(x); pi, e", "Angles in radians. Finite real arithmetic only. Exponentiation binds more tightly than unary minus. No code or scripts are executed.")
    )

    /** Evaluates finite SI inputs, rejecting invalid physical domains before applying a model.
     * @param id Stable utility ID.
     * @param raw Ordered field values, with engineering prefixes accepted by the shared parser.
     * @return Result with units or a readable validation error; no state or I/O is modified.
     */
    fun calculate(id: String, raw: List<String>): String = try {
        require(raw.size == all.firstOrNull { it.id == id }?.fields?.size) { "Enter every required field." }
        if (id == "scientific") Engineering.format(Expression(raw.single()).evaluate())
        else {
            val v = raw.map { Engineering.parse(it)?.takeIf(Double::isFinite) ?: error("Enter a valid number in every field.") }
            /** Positive input used for nonzero denominators and physical dimensions.
             * @param i Ordered field index from the selected model.
             * @return Validated scalar; invalid domains throw a readable argument error.
             */
            fun positive(i: Int): Double = v[i].also { require(it > 0) { "This model requires positive inputs." } }
            /** Nonnegative quantity allowing a valid zero result.
             * @param i Ordered field index from the selected model.
             * @return Validated scalar; invalid domains throw a readable argument error.
             */
            fun nonnegative(i: Int): Double = v[i].also { require(it >= 0) { "This model requires nonnegative inputs." } }
            /** Positive percentage at most 100, converted to a dimensionless factor.
             * @param i Ordered field index from the selected model.
             * @return Validated scalar; invalid domains throw a readable argument error.
             */
            fun percent(i: Int): Double = positive(i).also { require(it <= 100) { "Percentages must be above zero and at most 100." } } / 100
            when (id) {
                "transformer" -> Engineering.format(positive(0) * positive(2) / positive(1), "V")
                "ups" -> Engineering.format(positive(0) * positive(1) * percent(2) * percent(3) / positive(4), "h")
                "cable" -> Engineering.format(2 * positive(0) * positive(1) * positive(2) / positive(3), "mm²")
                "pf" -> (nonnegative(0) / (positive(1) * positive(2))).also { require(it <= 1) { "Real power cannot exceed apparent power in this model." } }.let { "PF = ${Engineering.format(it)}" }
                "energy" -> (nonnegative(0) * nonnegative(1) / 1000).let { "Energy: ${Engineering.format(it, "kWh")}\nCost: ${Engineering.format(it * nonnegative(2))} (entered currency)" }
                "temperature" -> { require(v[0] >= -273.15) { "Temperature is below absolute zero." }; "${Engineering.format(v[0] * 9 / 5 + 32, "°F")}\n${Engineering.format(v[0] + 273.15, "K")}" }
                else -> error("Unknown utility.")
            }
        }
    } catch (e: IllegalArgumentException) { e.message ?: "Invalid input." } catch (e: IllegalStateException) { e.message ?: "Invalid input." }
}

/** Bounded recursive-descent arithmetic parser; accepts a small mathematical grammar only.
 * @property text Expression supplied by the user, never passed to an interpreter.
 */
private class Expression(private val text: String) {
    /** Current parsing offset; length and recursion are bounded before evaluation. */
    private var index = 0

    /** Parses a complete expression, requiring finite real output.
     * @return Finite value; malformed input, excessive nesting and domain errors throw an argument error.
     */
    fun evaluate(): Double {
        require(text.length in 1..256 && text.count { it == '(' } <= 24) { "Use an expression of 1–256 characters with at most 24 groups." }
        val result = sum()
        whitespace()
        require(index == text.length && result.isFinite()) { "Invalid expression or non-finite result." }
        return result
    }

    /** Skips ordinary whitespace without accepting arbitrary tokens. @return Unit. */
    private fun whitespace() { while (index < text.length && text[index].isWhitespace()) index++ }

    /** Consumes one optional operator.
     * @param c Expected character.
     * @return True when consumed; false leaves the next non-space token untouched.
     */
    private fun eat(c: Char): Boolean { whitespace(); if (index < text.length && text[index] == c) { index++; return true }; return false }

    /** Parses addition/subtraction. @return Left-associative sum of terms. */
    private fun sum(): Double { var v = product(); while (true) v = when { eat('+') -> v + product(); eat('-') -> v - product(); else -> return v } }

    /** Parses multiplication/division. @return Left-associative product, rejecting division by zero. */
    private fun product(): Double { var v = unary(); while (true) v = when { eat('*') -> v * unary(); eat('/') -> { val d = unary(); require(d != 0.0) { "Division by zero." }; v / d }; else -> return v } }

    /** Parses unary signs with exponentiation precedence. @return Signed value. */
    private fun unary(): Double = when { eat('+') -> unary(); eat('-') -> -unary(); else -> power() }

    /** Parses right-associative exponentiation. @return Base raised to the optional exponent. */
    private fun power(): Double { val v = atom(); return if (eat('^')) v.pow(unary()) else v }

    /** Parses a number, named constant/function or parenthesized expression.
     * @return Real scalar; unknown functions and malformed numbers throw an argument error.
     */
    private fun atom(): Double {
        whitespace()
        if (eat('(')) { val v = sum(); require(eat(')')) { "Missing closing parenthesis." }; return v }
        val start = index
        while (index < text.length && text[index].isLetter()) index++
        if (index > start) {
            val name = text.substring(start, index)
            if (name == "pi") return PI
            if (name == "e") return E
            require(eat('(')) { "Functions require parentheses." }
            val v = sum(); require(eat(')')) { "Missing closing parenthesis." }
            return when(name) { "sqrt" -> sqrt(v); "sin" -> sin(v); "cos" -> cos(v); "tan" -> tan(v); "ln" -> ln(v); "log" -> log10(v); else -> throw IllegalArgumentException("Unknown function.") }
        }
        while (index < text.length && (text[index].isDigit() || text[index] == '.')) index++
        if (index < text.length && text[index] in "eE") {
            index++; if (index < text.length && text[index] in "+-") index++
            while (index < text.length && text[index].isDigit()) index++
        }
        return text.substring(start, index).toDoubleOrNull() ?: throw IllegalArgumentException("Expected a number.")
    }
}
````
