## app/src/test/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/UnitConversionsTests.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

import org.junit.Assert.*
import org.junit.Test

/** Dimensional examples exercise both SI prefix factors and affine temperature conversions. */
class UnitConversionsTests {
    /** @return Unit; representative conversions preserve magnitude and exact unit definitions. */
    @Test fun independentConversions() {
        assertEquals(3300.0, UnitConversions.convert("Voltage", "V", "mV", 3.3), 1e-9)
        assertEquals(0.001, UnitConversions.convert("Current", "mA", "A", 1.0), 1e-12)
        assertEquals(100.0, UnitConversions.convert("Temperature", "°F", "°C", 212.0), 1e-9)
        assertEquals(273.15, UnitConversions.convert("Temperature", "°C", "K", 0.0), 1e-9)
        assertEquals(25.4, UnitConversions.convert("Length", "in", "mm", 1.0), 1e-9)
        assertEquals(1000.0, UnitConversions.convert("Capacitance", "µF", "nF", 1.0), 1e-9)
    }
    /** @return Unit; cross-dimension units, non-finite scalars and impossible temperatures fail. */
    @Test fun invalidDomainsRejected() {
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException::class.java) { UnitConversions.convert("Voltage", "V", "A", 1.0) }
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException::class.java) { UnitConversions.convert("Temperature", "K", "°C", -1.0) }
        assertThrows(IllegalArgumentException::class.java) { UnitConversions.convert("Voltage", "V", "mV", Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY) }
    }
}
````

## app/src/test/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/WorkbenchToolsTests.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.domain

import org.junit.Assert.*
import org.junit.Test

/** Independent numeric examples and invalid domains exercise the new public utility models. */
class WorkbenchToolsTests {
    /** @return Unit; ideal transformer ratio must agree with independently calculated voltage. */
    @Test fun transformerRatio() { assertEquals("24 V", WorkbenchTools.calculate("transformer", listOf("240", "1000", "100"))) }
    /** @return Unit; runtime uses explicit discharge and efficiency factors rather than hidden defaults. */
    @Test fun upsAccountsForBothLossFactors() { assertEquals("4.8 h", WorkbenchTools.calculate("ups", listOf("24", "100", "50", "80", "200"))) }
    /** @return Unit; DC round-trip cable resistance must produce the independently derived area. */
    @Test fun cableSizingIncludesReturnPath() { assertEquals("3.5 mm²", WorkbenchTools.calculate("cable", listOf("10", "10", "0.0175", "1"))) }
    /** @return Unit; invalid power factor cannot be reported as a valid engineering result. */
    @Test fun invalidPowerFactorRejected() { assertTrue(WorkbenchTools.calculate("pf", listOf("500", "100", "2")).contains("cannot exceed")) }
    /** @return Unit; absolute zero is valid but lower thermodynamic temperature is rejected. */
    @Test fun temperatureBoundary() { assertTrue(WorkbenchTools.calculate("temperature", listOf("-273.15")).contains("0 K")); assertTrue(WorkbenchTools.calculate("temperature", listOf("-274")).contains("below absolute")) }
    /** @return Unit; parser precedence, radians and right-associative powers follow documented grammar. */
    @Test fun scientificGrammar() {
        assertEquals("19", WorkbenchTools.calculate("scientific", listOf("2+3^2+sqrt(64)")))
        assertEquals("512", WorkbenchTools.calculate("scientific", listOf("2^3^2")))
        assertEquals("-4", WorkbenchTools.calculate("scientific", listOf("-2^2")))
        assertEquals("1", WorkbenchTools.calculate("scientific", listOf("sin(pi/2)")))
    }
    /** @return Unit; malformed expressions, numerical overflow and zero divisors never escape as results. */
    @Test fun scientificInvalidInputs() {
        for (expression in listOf("1/0", "sqrt(-1)", "ln(0)", "1e999", "eval(1)", "1;2", "(".repeat(300))) {
            val output = WorkbenchTools.calculate("scientific", listOf(expression))
            assertFalse(output, output in listOf("NaN", "Infinity", "-Infinity"))
            assertTrue(output, output.any(Char::isLetter))
        }
    }
    /** @return Unit; percentages cannot silently exceed the stated model's physical range. */
    @Test fun invalidPercentagesRejected() { assertTrue(WorkbenchTools.calculate("ups", listOf("24", "100", "101", "80", "200")).contains("at most 100")) }
}
````

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.ui

import androidx.compose.ui.test.*
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createAndroidComposeRule
import com.electrokit.app.MainActivity
import org.junit.Assert.*
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

/**
 * Groups regression assertions for android ui regression tests; unexpected behaviour fails the test
 * visibly.
 */
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@Config(sdk = [34], qualifiers = "w360dp-h800dp")
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
class AndroidUiRegressionTests {
    /** Compose test rule owns Activity lifecycle and semantics synchronisation. */
    @get:Rule val ui = createAndroidComposeRule<MainActivity>()

    /**
     * Waits for asynchronous registry loading before querying semantics, avoiding startup race
     * failures.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    private fun ready() {
        ui.waitUntil(30_000) {
            ui.onAllNodesWithText("Tools").fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty()
        }
        ui.onNodeWithText("Tools").performClick()
    }

    /**
     * Uses visible catalogue search rather than brittle row indices or scroll positions to open a
     * calculator.
     *
     * @param title Visible calculator title used to select the intended test route.
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    private fun openCalculator(title: String) {
        ready()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search")).performTextReplacement(title)
        ui.onNode(hasText(title) and !hasSetTextAction()).performClick()
        ui.waitForIdle()
    }

    /**
     * Targets the editable node by its visible label so the test follows the actual user input
     * path.
     *
     * @param label Visible field/cell caption used for accessible presentation.
     * @param value Input scalar in the operation’s documented units.
     * @return A finite scalar in the expected field unit, or null for incompatible units/invalid
     *   input. Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws
     *   IOException while enabled.
     */
    private fun input(label: String, value: String) {
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText(label)).performTextReplacement(value)
    }

    /** A cached explicit result must not survive a mode change with different physical behavior.
     * @return Unit; at t=0 a 5 V capacitor model changes from 0 V charge to 5 V discharge.
     */
    @Test fun calculationModeChangeInvalidatesExplicitResult() {
        openCalculator("Capacitor charge")
        ui.onNode(hasText("Mode:", substring = true)).performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Charge").performClick()
        input("Initial / supply voltage", "5")
        input("Elapsed time", "0")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Calculate").performScrollTo().performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Voltage: 0 V", substring = true).assertExists()
        ui.onNode(hasText("Mode:", substring = true)).performScrollTo().performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Discharge").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Voltage: 5 V", substring = true).assertExists()
    }

    /**
     * Verifies main tabs and reference navigation work; unexpected behaviour fails the test
     * visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun mainTabsAndReferenceNavigationWork() {
        ready()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Pin-outs").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("USB port").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Universal Serial Bus").assertExists()
        ui.onNode(verticalList())
            .performScrollToNode(hasText("USB 3.x", substring = true))
        ui.onNodeWithText("USB 3.x Standard-A").assertIsDisplayed()
        ui.runOnIdle { ui.activity.onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }
        ui.onNodeWithText("Reference").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Resistivity Table").performClick()
        ui.onAllNodesWithText("Resistivity Table").assertCountEquals(2)
    }

    /**
     * Verifies extreme ratio is an inline error instead of a crash; unexpected behaviour fails the
     * test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun extremeRatioIsAnInlineErrorInsteadOfACrash() {
        openCalculator("Resistor Ratio")
        input("Target R2/R1", "1e9")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Target ratio must be between", substring = true).assertExists()
        input("Target R2/R1", "1e-9")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Target ratio must be between", substring = true).assertExists()
        input("Target R2/R1", "2.5")
        ui.onNodeWithText("R1:", substring = true).assertExists()
    }

    /**
     * Verifies selected kilo unit does not multiply a suffixed value twice; unexpected behaviour
     * fails the test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun selectedKiloUnitDoesNotMultiplyASuffixedValueTwice() {
        openCalculator("Ohm’s Law")
        // Resistance has the only unit selector initially labelled Ω.
        ui.onNodeWithText("Ω", substring = false).performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("kΩ", substring = false).performClick()
        input("Resistance", "10k")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Typed suffix / unit used; selector ignored").assertExists()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Resistance: 10 kΩ", substring = true).assertExists()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Current: 1.2 mA", substring = true).assertExists()
    }

    /**
     * Verifies fractional tolerance uses percent text; unexpected behaviour fails the test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun fractionalToleranceUsesPercentText() {
        openCalculator("Resistor Colour Code")
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Green tol ±0.5 percent").performScrollTo().performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("1.1 kΩ ±0.5%").assertExists()
        ui.onNodeWithText("500 m%", substring = true).assertDoesNotExist()
    }

    /**
     * Verifies calculator input survives activity recreation; unexpected behaviour fails the test
     * visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun calculatorInputSurvivesActivityRecreation() {
        openCalculator("Voltage divider")
        input("Input voltage", "24")
        org.robolectric.RuntimeEnvironment.setQualifiers("w800dp-h360dp-land")
        ui.activityRule.scenario.recreate()
        ui.waitForIdle()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Input voltage")).assertTextContains("24")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Vout: 12 V", substring = true).assertExists()
    }

    /**
     * Verifies light theme persists across activity recreation; unexpected behaviour fails the test
     * visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun lightThemePersistsAcrossActivityRecreation() {
        ready()
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Menu").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasText("Settings") and hasClickAction() and !hasAnyAncestor(hasTestTag("main_navigation"))).performClick()
        // Establish a dark baseline: other preview tests deliberately persist a light preference.
        if (ui.onAllNodes(isOn()).fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty()) {
            ui.onNode(isToggleable()).performClick()
            ui.waitUntil(10_000) { ui.onAllNodes(isOff()).fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() }
        }
        ui.onNode(isToggleable()).assertIsOff().performClick()
        ui.waitUntil(10_000) { ui.onAllNodes(isOn()).fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() }
        ui.onNode(isToggleable()).assertIsOn()
        ui.activityRule.scenario.recreate()
        ui.waitForIdle()
        ui.onNode(isToggleable()).assertIsOn()
    }

    /**
     * Verifies every catalogue entry opens without crashing; unexpected behaviour fails the test
     * visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun everyCatalogueEntryOpensWithoutCrashing() {
        ready()
        val repository =
            com.electrokit.app.data.Repository(org.robolectric.RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication())
        kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking { repository.loadAssets() }
        var opened = 0
        for (tab in listOf("CALCULATORS", "PIN-OUTS", "RESOURCES")) {
            ui.onNodeWithText(mapOf("CALCULATORS" to "Tools", "PIN-OUTS" to "Pin-outs", "RESOURCES" to "Reference").getValue(tab)).performClick()
            ui.waitForIdle()
            for (entry in repository.registry.filter { it.tab == tab }) {
                ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search"))
                    .performTextReplacement(entry.title)
                ui.onNode(hasText(entry.title) and !hasSetTextAction()).performClick()
                ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Back").assertIsDisplayed()
                ui.onAllNodesWithText(entry.title).assertAny(hasText(entry.title))
                ui.runOnIdle { ui.activity.onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }
                ui.waitForIdle()
                opened++
            }
        }
        assertEquals(107, opened)
    }

    /**
     * Verifies bundled databases open without enablement and retain working filters; unexpected
     * behaviour fails the test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun bundledDatabasesAlwaysOpenAndSearch() {
        ready()
        val repository =
            com.electrokit.app.data.Repository(org.robolectric.RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication())
        kotlinx.coroutines.runBlocking {
            repository.loadAssets()
            repository.update { it.copy(modules = emptySet()) }
        }
        ui.onNodeWithText("34 calculators", substring = true).assertExists()
        ui.onAllNodesWithText("Data").onLast().performClick()
        for (entry in repository.registry.filter { it.tab == "PLUGINS" }) {
            ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search databases"))
                .performTextReplacement(entry.title)
            ui.onNodeWithText("ENABLE").assertDoesNotExist()
            ui.onNodeWithText("DISABLE").assertDoesNotExist()
            ui.onNodeWithText("OPEN DATABASE", substring = true).performClick()
            ui.onNodeWithText("Numeric parameter: Any").assertExists()
            val name = repository.parts.getValue(entry.id).first().name
            ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search")).performTextReplacement(name)
            ui.onNode(hasText(name) and !hasSetTextAction()).performClick()
            ui.onNodeWithText("Product reference:", substring = true).assertExists()
            if (entry.id == "m1") {
                ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search")).performTextClearance()
                ui.onNodeWithText("Numeric parameter: Any").performClick()
                ui.onNodeWithText("Output V").performClick()
                input("Minimum", "-12")
                input("Maximum", "0")
                ui.onNodeWithText("LM7905").assertExists()
                ui.onNodeWithText("LM7912").assertExists()
                ui.onNodeWithText("LM7805").assertDoesNotExist()
            }
            ui.runOnIdle { ui.activity.onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }
            ui.waitForIdle()
        }
    }

    /**
     * Verifies large text keeps main actions reachable; unexpected behaviour fails the test
     * visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun largeTextKeepsMainActionsReachable() {
        org.robolectric.RuntimeEnvironment.setFontScale(2f)
        ui.activityRule.scenario.recreate()
        ready()
        assertEquals(2f, ui.activity.resources.configuration.fontScale, 0f)
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Info").assertIsDisplayed().performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("WHAT’S INCLUDED").assertIsDisplayed().performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Resistor Colour Code").assertExists()
    }

    /**
     * Ensures the catalogue uses the bottom viewport instead of reserving the old 56 dp footer.
     *
     * @return Unit; the measured viewport includes only ordinary system-navigation clearance.
     * @throws AssertionError if a persistent empty footer reduces the list viewport.
     */
    @Test
    fun catalogueHasNoReservedBottomFooter() {
        ready()
        val rootBounds = ui.onRoot().fetchSemanticsNode().boundsInRoot
        val listBounds =
            ui.onAllNodes(verticalList())
                .fetchSemanticsNodes()
                .first {
                    it.boundsInRoot.center.x > 0 && it.boundsInRoot.center.x < rootBounds.width
                }
                .boundsInRoot
        val navigation = ui.onNodeWithTag("main_navigation").assertIsDisplayed().fetchSemanticsNode().boundsInRoot
        val density = ui.activity.resources.displayMetrics.density
        // Visible navigation is functional UI; separate blank strips remain regressions.
        val listGap = kotlin.math.abs(navigation.top - listBounds.bottom) / density
        val systemGap = (rootBounds.bottom - navigation.bottom) / density
        assertTrue("Empty strip before navigation: $listGap dp", listGap <= 1f)
        assertTrue("Unexpected empty footer: $systemGap dp", systemGap <= 48f)
    }
}
````

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.ui

import androidx.compose.ui.test.*
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createAndroidComposeRule
import com.electrokit.app.MainActivity
import java.io.File
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

/**
 * Groups regression assertions for design preview tests; unexpected behaviour fails the test
 * visibly.
 */
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@Config(sdk = [34], qualifiers = "w412dp-h915dp")
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
class DesignPreviewTests {
    /** Compose test rule owns Activity lifecycle and semantics synchronisation. */
    @get:Rule val ui = createAndroidComposeRule<MainActivity>()

    /**
     * Waits for asynchronous registry loading before querying semantics, avoiding startup race
     * failures.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    private fun ready() {
        ui.waitUntil(30000) {
            ui.onAllNodesWithText("Tools").fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty()
        }
        ui.onNodeWithText("Tools").performClick()
    }

    /**
     * Waits for navigation animation then draws the actual decor view, avoiding unsupported
     * PixelCopy in Robolectric.
     *
     * @param name Asset filename or preview output name, as stated by the operation.
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    private fun save(name: String) {
        ui.mainClock.advanceTimeBy(1000)
        ui.waitForIdle()
        val folder = File("build/design-previews")
        folder.mkdirs()
        ui.runOnIdle {
            val view = ui.activity.window.decorView
            val bitmap =
                android.graphics.Bitmap.createBitmap(
                    view.width,
                    view.height,
                    android.graphics.Bitmap.Config.ARGB_8888,
                )
            view.draw(android.graphics.Canvas(bitmap))
            File(folder, name + ".png").outputStream().use {
                bitmap.compress(android.graphics.Bitmap.CompressFormat.PNG, 100, it)
            }
            bitmap.recycle()
        }
    }

    /**
     * Sets the requested palette only when necessary so prior saved test state cannot invert the
     * desired preview.
     *
     * @param light True selects the light palette.
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    private fun theme(light: Boolean) {
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Menu").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasText("Settings") and hasClickAction() and !hasAnyAncestor(hasTestTag("main_navigation"))).performClick()
        val wanted =
            if (light) androidx.compose.ui.state.ToggleableState.On
            else androidx.compose.ui.state.ToggleableState.Off
        val toggle = ui.onNode(isToggleable())
        if (
            toggle
                .fetchSemanticsNode()
                .config[androidx.compose.ui.semantics.SemanticsProperties.ToggleableState] != wanted
        )
            toggle.performClick()
        ui.waitUntil(10000) {
            ui.onNode(isToggleable())
                .fetchSemanticsNode()
                .config[androidx.compose.ui.semantics.SemanticsProperties.ToggleableState] == wanted
        }
        ui.runOnIdle { ui.activity.onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }
        ui.waitForIdle()
    }

    /**
     * Verifies home preview; unexpected behaviour fails the test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun homePreview() {
        ready()
        theme(false)
        save("home")
        theme(true)
        save("light")
    }

    /**
     * Verifies connector preview; unexpected behaviour fails the test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun connectorPreview() {
        ready()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Pin-outs").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("USB port").performClick()
        save("usb")
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search this reference"))
            .performTextReplacement("USB 1")
        save("table")
    }

    /**
     * Captures the actual new connector families in both palettes to reveal clipping and contrast
     * issues.
     *
     * @return Unit; missing routes, inaccessible search fields and rendering failures fail the
     *   test.
     */
    @Test
    fun illustratedReferencePreviews() {
        ready()
        theme(true)
        ui.onNodeWithText("Pin-outs").performClick()
        for ((title, filename) in
            listOf(
                "Serial port" to "serial-illustration",
                "ATX Power connectors" to "power-illustration",
                "Arduino Uno board" to "uno-illustration",
                "RCA connector" to "rca-illustration",
                "VGA connector" to "vga-illustration",
                "Fibre optic cable colour" to "fibre-table",
            )) {
            ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction()).performTextReplacement(title)
            ui.onNode(hasText(title) and !hasSetTextAction(), useUnmergedTree = true).performClick()
            save(filename)
            if (filename == "serial-illustration") {
                ui.onAllNodesWithText("Enlarge diagram")[0].performScrollTo().performClick()
                ui.onNodeWithText("Close diagram").assertIsDisplayed()
                ui.onNodeWithText("Close diagram").performClick()
            }
            ui.runOnIdle { ui.activity.onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }
            ui.waitForIdle()
        }
    }
}
````

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.ui

import androidx.compose.ui.test.*
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createAndroidComposeRule
import com.electrokit.app.MainActivity
import java.io.File
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

/** Actual Compose navigation/search/bookmark and drawing checks in simulated API-34 Android. */
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@Config(sdk = [34], qualifiers = "w412dp-h915dp")
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
class EngineeringUiTests {
    /** Activity lifecycle and Compose semantics rule. */
    @get:Rule val ui = createAndroidComposeRule<MainActivity>()

    /** Checks all five destinations are visible without an undiscoverable horizontal tab scroll.
     * @return Unit; clipped or missing navigation labels fail the assertions.
     */
    @Test fun allHomeTabsVisible() {
        ui.waitUntil(30000) { ui.onAllNodesWithText("Tools").fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() }
        listOf("Home", "Tools", "Learn", "Favorites", "Settings").forEach {
            ui.onAllNodesWithText(it).onLast().assertIsDisplayed()
        }
    }

    /** Exercises the engineering dashboard in persisted light mode and records actual simulated rendering.
     * @return Unit; theme persistence or module navigation failures fail this test.
     */
    @Test fun lightEngineeringPreview() {
        ui.waitUntil(30000) { ui.onAllNodesWithText("Tools").fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() }
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Menu").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasText("Settings") and hasClickAction() and !hasAnyAncestor(hasTestTag("main_navigation"))).performClick()
        val toggle = ui.onNode(isToggleable())
        // Force a real save even when another test's in-memory DataStore already selected light.
        if (toggle.fetchSemanticsNode().config[androidx.compose.ui.semantics.SemanticsProperties.ToggleableState] == androidx.compose.ui.state.ToggleableState.On) {
            toggle.performClick()
            ui.waitUntil(30000) { toggle.fetchSemanticsNode().config[androidx.compose.ui.semantics.SemanticsProperties.ToggleableState] == androidx.compose.ui.state.ToggleableState.Off }
        }
        toggle.performClick()
        ui.waitUntil(30000) { com.electrokit.app.data.StartupTheme.light(ui.activity) }
        ui.runOnIdle { ui.activity.onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }
        ui.activityRule.scenario.recreate()
        home()
        save("dashboard-light")
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction()).performTextReplacement("Motor shaft torque")
````

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.ui

/** Selects the actual content list rather than a horizontally scrolling category row.
````

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.ui

import androidx.compose.ui.test.*
import androidx.compose.ui.test.junit4.createAndroidComposeRule
import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModelProvider
import com.electrokit.app.MainActivity
import com.electrokit.app.viewmodel.EngineeringAccess
import org.junit.Assert.*
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config
import org.robolectric.annotation.GraphicsMode

/** Exercises redesigned native navigation, privacy boundary and bundled images in simulated Android. */
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@Config(sdk = [34], qualifiers = "w412dp-h915dp")
@GraphicsMode(GraphicsMode.Mode.NATIVE)
class WorkbenchUiTests {
    /** Owns the Activity and Compose synchronization for each test. */
    @get:Rule val ui = createAndroidComposeRule<MainActivity>()

    /** @return Unit; waits for actual repository loading rather than treating a process as readiness. */
    private fun ready() { ui.waitUntil(30000) { ui.onAllNodesWithText("Tools").fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() } }

    /** @return Unit; opens the guarded destination using public navigation. */
    private fun engineering() { ready(); ui.onNodeWithText("Tools").performClick(); ui.onNodeWithText("Engineering").performClick() }

    /** @return Unit; incorrect input cannot reveal snippets, and manual locking removes composed data. */
    @Test fun protectedContentRequiresCodeAndRelocks() {
        engineering()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Engineering access").assertIsDisplayed()
        ui.onNodeWithText("E217", substring = true).assertDoesNotExist()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Access code")).performTextReplacement("000")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Unlock").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Access code not accepted.").assertIsDisplayed()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Access code")).performTextReplacement("789")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Unlock").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search all engineering references and tools")).assertExists()
        ui.activityRule.scenario.recreate()
        ui.waitForIdle()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Lock engineering").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Engineering access").assertIsDisplayed()
        ui.onNode(hasText("Search all engineering references and tools")).assertDoesNotExist()
    }

    /** @return Unit; activity-local state never becomes a persisted grant for a fresh session. */
    @Test fun accessIsNotSavedAndAttemptsAreRateLimited() {
        val access = ViewModelProvider(ui.activity)[EngineeringAccess::class.java]
        assertFalse(access.unlocked)
        assertNull(access.unlock("789")); assertTrue(access.unlocked)
        access.lock(); assertFalse(access.unlocked)
        repeat(5) { assertNotNull(access.unlock("000")) }
        assertTrue(access.unlock("789")!!.contains("Wait"))
        assertFalse(EngineeringAccess().unlocked)
    }

    /** @return Unit; protected fault text cannot leak through the public dashboard search. */
    @Test fun publicSearchExcludesFaultSnippets() {
        ready()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search")).performTextReplacement("E217")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Drive Chain Switch", substring = true).assertDoesNotExist()
        ui.onNodeWithText("E217 — Drive Chain Switch").assertDoesNotExist()
    }

    /** @return Unit; a new public model calculates through its native inputs and Android Back returns to Tools. */
    @Test fun utilityCalculationAndAndroidBack() {
        ready(); ui.onNodeWithText("Tools").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasScrollToIndexAction() and SemanticsMatcher.keyIsDefined(androidx.compose.ui.semantics.SemanticsProperties.HorizontalScrollAxisRange))
            .performScrollToNode(hasText("Utilities"))
        ui.onNodeWithText("Utilities").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Ideal transformer").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Primary voltage (V)")).performTextReplacement("240")
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Primary turns")).performTextReplacement("1000")
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Secondary turns")).performTextReplacement("100")
        ui.onNodeWithText("Calculate").performScrollTo().performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("24 V").assertExists()
        ui.runOnIdle { ui.activity.onBackPressedDispatcher.onBackPressed() }
        ui.onNodeWithText("Engineering unit converter").assertExists()
    }

    /** @return Unit; selected units govern the actual converter input and output without duplicate prefix scaling. */
    @Test fun unitConverterNativeWorkflow() {
        ready(); ui.onNodeWithText("Tools").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasScrollToIndexAction() and SemanticsMatcher.keyIsDefined(androidx.compose.ui.semantics.SemanticsProperties.HorizontalScrollAxisRange))
            .performScrollToNode(hasText("Utilities"))
        ui.onNodeWithText("Utilities").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Engineering unit converter").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Value")).performTextReplacement("3.3")

        ui.onNodeWithText("Quantity: Voltage").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Temperature").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Value")).performTextReplacement("100")

    /** @return Unit; an actual bundled image renders and a component favorite is navigable. */
    @Test fun componentImageAndFavoriteRoundTrip() {
        ready(); ui.onNodeWithText("Learn").performClick()
        ui.onNode(hasSetTextAction() and hasText("Search")).performTextReplacement("Axial Resistor")
        ui.waitUntil(10000) { ui.onAllNodes(hasText("Axial Resistor") and !hasSetTextAction()).fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() }
        ui.onNode(hasText("Axial Resistor") and !hasSetTextAction()).performClick()
        ui.waitUntil(10000) { ui.onAllNodesWithContentDescription("Axial Resistor").fetchSemanticsNodes().isNotEmpty() }
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Axial Resistor").assertExists()
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Favorite component").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithContentDescription("Back").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Favorites").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Axial Resistor").assertExists()

    /** @return Unit; the native home render is exported from the simulated Activity for visual review. */
    @Test fun homeScreenshotAndSystemBarFlags() {
        ready()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Settings").performClick()
        ui.onNodeWithText("Dark").performClick()
        ui.waitUntil(10000) { !com.electrokit.app.data.StartupTheme.light(ui.activity) }
        ui.onNodeWithText("Home").performClick()
        ui.mainClock.advanceTimeBy(1000)
        ui.runOnIdle {
            assertEquals(0, ui.activity.window.attributes.flags and android.view.WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_FULLSCREEN)

            view.draw(android.graphics.Canvas(bitmap))

            file.parentFile!!.mkdirs()
            file.outputStream().use { bitmap.compress(android.graphics.Bitmap.CompressFormat.PNG, 100, it) }
            bitmap.recycle()
        }
    }
````

## app/src/testDebug/java/com/electrokit/app/viewmodel/InputJournalTests.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.viewmodel

import com.electrokit.app.data.InputJournal
import java.io.File
import org.junit.Assert.*
import org.junit.Rule
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.rules.TemporaryFolder
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config

/** Exercises actual atomic-file persistence rather than an in-memory staging fixture. */
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@Config(sdk = [34])
class InputJournalTests {
    /** Private temporary files isolate journal recovery from application preferences. */
    @get:Rule val folder = TemporaryFolder()

    /**
     * A completed staging call must be readable by a newly constructed store.
     *
     * @return Unit; disk/read-back mismatches fail the test.
     */
    @Test
    fun stagedInputsSurviveNewJournalInstance() {
        val file = File(folder.root, "inputs.json")
        InputJournal(file).put("c4", mapOf("v" to "24", "unit_r" to "3"))
        assertEquals(mapOf("v" to "24", "unit_r" to "3"), InputJournal(file).read()["c4"])
    }

    /**
     * Acknowledging an older DataStore write must not delete a newer staged edit.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertions detect lost updates or failed acknowledgement cleanup.
     */
    @Test
    fun acknowledgementRetainsNewerEdits() {
        val journal = InputJournal(File(folder.root, "inputs.json"))
        journal.put("c4", mapOf("v" to "12"))
        val old = journal.read()
        journal.put("c4", mapOf("v" to "24"))
        journal.clear(old)
        assertEquals("24", journal.read()["c4"]?.get("v"))
        journal.clear(journal.read())
        assertTrue(journal.read().isEmpty())
    }

    /**
     * Damaged backup text must produce an error instead of silently discarding unsaved work.
     *
     * @return Unit; expected IOException confirms corruption is surfaced.
     */
    @Test(expected = java.io.IOException::class)
    fun corruptJournalIsNotSilentlyReplaced() {
        val file = File(folder.root, "inputs.json")
        file.writeText("broken")
        InputJournal(file).read()
    }
    /** @return Unit; damaged JSON survives quarantine and a later explicit retry can save again. */
    @Test
    fun corruptJournalIsPreservedAndRetryCanContinue() {
        val path = File(folder.root, "broken.json")
        path.writeText("{broken")
        val journal = InputJournal(path)
        try { journal.read(); fail("Expected visible corruption error") } catch (_: java.io.IOException) { }
        assertTrue(folder.root.listFiles()!!.any { it.name.startsWith("broken.json.corrupt-") && it.readText() == "{broken" })
        journal.put("c4", mapOf("v" to "12"))
        assertEquals("12", journal.read()["c4"]?.get("v"))
    }

}

````

## app/src/testDebug/java/com/electrokit/app/viewmodel/RetryRegressionTests.kt

````kotlin
package com.electrokit.app.viewmodel

import android.os.Looper
import com.electrokit.app.data.*
import kotlinx.coroutines.flow.MutableStateFlow
import org.junit.Assert.*
import org.junit.Test
import org.junit.runner.RunWith
import org.robolectric.RobolectricTestRunner
import org.robolectric.RuntimeEnvironment
import org.robolectric.Shadows.shadowOf
import org.robolectric.annotation.Config

/**
 * Groups regression assertions for retry regression tests; unexpected behaviour fails the test
 * visibly.
 */
@RunWith(RobolectricTestRunner::class)
@Config(sdk = [34])
class RetryRegressionTests {
    /**
     * Groups regression assertions for failing repository; unexpected behaviour fails the test
     * visibly.
     */
    private class FailingRepository : AppRepository {
        /** Ordered routes published only after every asset decodes. */
        override val registry = emptyList<Entry>()
        /** Shared reference content keyed by stable content ID. */
        override val pages = emptyMap<String, Page>()
        /** Bundled component datasets keyed by module ID. */
        override val parts = emptyMap<String, List<Part>>()
        /** Preference observation owned by storage and exposed read-only by the ViewModel. */
        override val preferences = MutableStateFlow(PreferencesState())
        /** Enables deterministic simulated write failure without touching real disk data. */
        var fail = true
        /** Counts writes so an unrelated empty flush cannot pass a retry test. */
        var attempts = 0
        /** Captures the real staging thread for the production-dispatcher regression. */
        @Volatile var stageOnMain: Boolean? = null
        /** Optional broken asset load isolates error ownership from successful input persistence. */
        var failLoad = false

        /** Staged snapshot survives creation of another ViewModel using this fixture. */
        private val staged = mutableMapOf<String, Map<String, String>>()

        /**
         * Stages before the asynchronous write.
         *
         * @param id Calculator key.
         * @param values Raw fields.
         * @return Unit; the fixture staging operation succeeds.
         */
        override fun stageInputs(id: String, values: Map<String, String>) {
            stageOnMain = Looper.myLooper() == Looper.getMainLooper()
            staged[id] = values.toMap()
        }

        /**
         * Returns staged fields for process-recreation assertions.
         *
         * @return Snapshot map; no failure is simulated here.
         */
        override fun stagedInputs() = staged.toMap()

        /**
         * Removes only acknowledged values.
         *
         * @param committed Main-record snapshot.
         * @return Unit; newer staged values remain.
         */
        override fun clearStagedInputs(committed: Map<String, Map<String, String>>) {
            committed.forEach { (id, values) -> if (staged[id] == values) staged.remove(id) }
        }

        /**
         * Verifies load assets; unexpected behaviour fails the test visibly.
         *
         * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
         *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws
         *   IOException while enabled.
         */
        override suspend fun loadAssets() { if (failLoad) throw java.io.IOException("Load failure") }

        /**
         * Verifies reset preferences; unexpected behaviour fails the test visibly.
         *
         * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
         *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws
         *   IOException while enabled.
         */
        override suspend fun resetPreferences() {
            preferences.value = PreferencesState()
        }

        /**
         * Verifies update; unexpected behaviour fails the test visibly.
         *
         * @param transform Atomic transformation of the latest persisted snapshot.
         * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
         *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws
         *   IOException while enabled.
         */
        override suspend fun update(transform: (PreferencesState) -> PreferencesState) {
            attempts++
            if (fail) throw java.io.IOException("Simulated disk failure")
            preferences.value = transform(preferences.value)
        }
    }

    /**
     * Verifies settings retry repeats settings mutation rather than flushing inputs; unexpected
     * behaviour fails the test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun settingsRetryRepeatsSettingsMutationRatherThanFlushingInputs() {
        val repository = FailingRepository()
        val vm = AppViewModel(RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication(), repository, kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers.Unconfined)
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        vm.theme(true)
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        assertNotNull(vm.error.value)
        assertEquals(1, repository.attempts)
        repository.fail = false
        vm.retryFailedAction()
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        assertEquals(2, repository.attempts)
        assertTrue(repository.preferences.value.light)
        assertNull(vm.error.value)
    }

    /**
     * Verifies input retry persists pending snapshot; unexpected behaviour fails the test visibly.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures identify regressions and are never swallowed.
     *   Assertion/time-out failures propagate; the failure fixture deliberately throws IOException
     *   while enabled.
     */
    @Test
    fun inputRetryPersistsPendingSnapshot() {
        val repository = FailingRepository()
        val vm = AppViewModel(RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication(), repository, kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers.Unconfined)
        vm.values("c4", mapOf("v" to "24"))
        vm.flushInputs()
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        assertNotNull(vm.error.value)
        repository.fail = false
        vm.retryFailedAction()
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        assertEquals("24", repository.preferences.value.values["c4"]?.get("v"))
        assertNull(vm.error.value)
    }

    /**
     * Verifies a staged edit is visible to a fresh ViewModel despite a failed main-record write.
     *
     * @return Unit; assertion failures expose a lost-input regression.
     */
    @Test
    fun freshViewModelRecoversStagedInputsBeforeDataStoreCommit() {
        val repository = FailingRepository()
        val first = AppViewModel(RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication(), repository, kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers.Unconfined)
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        first.values("c4", mapOf("v" to "37"))
        assertEquals("37", repository.stagedInputs()["c4"]?.get("v"))
        val restored = AppViewModel(RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication(), repository, kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers.Unconfined)
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        assertEquals("37", restored.preferences.value.values["c4"]?.get("v"))
    }
    /** @return Unit; a successful input transaction must not hide a failed asset load. */
    @Test
    fun inputSuccessDoesNotDismissLoadFailure() {
        val repository = FailingRepository().apply { fail = false; failLoad = true }
        val vm = AppViewModel(RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication(), repository, kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers.Unconfined)
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        val loadError = vm.error.value
        assertNotNull(loadError)
        vm.values("c4", mapOf("v" to "24"))
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        assertEquals(loadError, vm.error.value)
        repository.failLoad = false
        vm.retryFailedAction()
        shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
        assertTrue(vm.loaded.value)
    }

    /** @return Unit; actual production dispatcher must move blocking journal work off main. */
    @Test
    fun productionJournalRunsOffMainThread() {
        val repository = FailingRepository().apply { fail = false }
        val vm = AppViewModel(RuntimeEnvironment.getApplication(), repository)
        vm.values("c4", mapOf("v" to "24"))
        val deadline = System.nanoTime() + 5_000_000_000L
        while (repository.stageOnMain == null && System.nanoTime() < deadline) {
            shadowOf(Looper.getMainLooper()).idle()
            Thread.sleep(5)
        }
        assertEquals(false, repository.stageOnMain)
    }

}

````

## docs/ANDROID_PHONE_BUILD_GUIDE.md

````markdown
# Phone-only development

GitHub Actions provides the build machine; Android Studio is not required on the phone.

1. Open the repository in the GitHub app/mobile browser. Create/select a feature branch from main.
2. Use GitHub's file editor or browser editor to change actual source files. Preserve directory structure; root documents alone cannot build Android.
3. Preview the diff, commit with a descriptive message and open a pull request.
4. Open Checks/Actions and select the run for the exact branch and commit. Inspect failed step logs; distinguish downloads/SDK failures from compiler and assertion errors.
5. After a successful Android CI run, download its debug artifact ZIP while signed in. Extract it in Files and open `app-debug.apk`.
6. Allow installation from the browser/Files app only as needed. Debug signing may not match your installed release; preserve valuable installed data.
7. For production, configure the original signing secrets, use the release workflow, then download the signed APK from Releases and verify its version/update compatibility.
8. Revert broken changes with a revert commit/pull request and rerun CI. Do not force-push main.

Manual builds: Actions → **Android CI** → **Run workflow**, choose the branch and run. The release workflow has a separate manual trigger and refuses unsigned publication.

Browser editing provides no local compiler, debugger or emulator. Large refactors, conflicts and accessibility review are harder on a phone. Use CI reports and physical-device checks. Never put keystore passwords into source, issues or chat; use repository Actions secrets.

````

## docs/ARCHITECTURE.md

````markdown
# Architecture

The existing stack remains: one `MainActivity`, Kotlin, Compose Material 3, Navigation Compose, DataStore Preferences and kotlinx.serialization. No image-loading framework, cloud service or additional database was introduced.

`MainActivity.kt` selects effective appearance, configures visible edge-to-edge system bars and composes `ElectroApp`. `ui/screens/App.kt` retains `main`, `entry/{id}`, `engineering/{route}`, `settings`, `plugins` and `info/{tab}` routes. `WorkbenchScreen.kt` supplies five primary destinations and saveable local component/lesson/utility selection.

Original calculation engines and IDs remain. `WorkbenchTools.kt` adds seven explicit educational models and a bounded arithmetic parser; it never evaluates executable code. `UnitConversions.kt` separates physical dimensions and temperature offsets.

`Repository.kt` retains the application-scoped `electrokit` DataStore and existing raw-input journal. New appearance mode, recent public IDs and bounded saved-result snapshots have default values for compatibility. Malformed saved state is surfaced rather than silently discarded.

`ComponentLibrary.kt` owns local metadata and generic lesson content. PNGs decode on Dispatchers.IO at display resolution and use a bounded 8 MiB cache. Failed assets have readable fallbacks. Artwork does not establish exact product identity or ratings.

`EngineeringScreen` and escalator image pages wrap `EngineeringGate` before composing protected data. The shared `EngineeringAccess` Activity ViewModel never persists an unlocked grant. Rotation retains that ViewModel; a fresh Activity/process starts locked. Public search/favorites omit protected snippets while locked. Secure-window protection applies while the gate is composed. APK assets remain extractable, so the gate is not encryption.

Application ID `com.electrokit.app`, minSdk 24, compile/target SDK 35 and release signing names remain. No Internet permission or deep-link filters are added. Only the launcher Activity is exported. Backups remain disabled. Real device/system-bar, TalkBack and upgrade checks remain distinct from Robolectric simulation.

````

## docs/AUDIT_REPORT.md

````markdown
# Audit and boundaries

At remote `91f9725`, the checkout had root scripts/docs and 66 `photos/` PNGs but lacked nested Android files. Original files were recovered from `FULL_SOURCE.md` only after matching bytes to the original SHA-256 manifest. The Base64 wrapper also matched Gradle's upstream JAR. Recovery is a separate commit.

Preserved: application ID, SDK bounds, datastore/journal identity, old preference keys, registry IDs, original calculation engines and exact fault/source rows. New preference fields are additive. All controller routes and escalator image pages use a shared session boundary.

Confirmed corrections: explicit immersive bar hiding removed; scroll-triggered header hiding removed; complete project structure restored; executable wrapper and distribution checksum supplied; writable cloud caches configured without disabling TLS; Git internals/venvs excluded from packaging; large-font navigation overflow corrected; bounded off-thread image decoding added.

Known limits:

- Three-digit access is basic UI restriction, not encryption; APK assets and verification code remain reverse-engineerable.
- Generated images do not establish manufacturer identity, ratings or terminals. Many device-specific specifications/test procedures were not supplied. Pages identify that gap.
- TI and Modbus retrieval attempts returned 403 under cloud network policy. New citations were not independently downloaded/verified; generic lessons are not certified operational wiring instructions.
- English only; new workbench text needs resource extraction before additional translations.
- Scientific arithmetic is not a computer algebra system. Cable sizing models voltage drop, not full standards-based selection/protection.
- No original release key, real-device installation, upgrade migration, TalkBack speech or hardware checks were available.
- Recovered `verification/` records are historical. Use current `app/build/` outputs and `BUILD_REPORT.md` for this run.

No claim is made that every manufacturer pinout, component model or language is fully documented or certified.
````

## docs/COMMANDS.md

````markdown
# Command reference

Unless stated otherwise, run from the repository root `electro`. Requirements: Git, JDK 17, SDK Platform 35/Build Tools 35.0.0/platform-tools, and network access for first dependency downloads. Kotlin/Gradle/AGP come from committed pins. Replace placeholder repository/branch names deliberately.

| Purpose | Bash | PowerShell | Expected result / common error |
|---|---|---|---|
| Clone (run in parent directory) | `git clone https://github.com/nandurpm/electro.git` | Same | New `electro/`; access errors require checking existing GitHub access |
| Enter checkout | `cd electro` | `Set-Location electro` | Commands now address project root |
| Check changes | `git status --short` | Same | Lists changed/untracked files; preserve these before pulling |
| Fetch | `git fetch origin` | Same | Remote refs refreshed, working files preserved |
| Update clean main | `git switch main` then `git pull --ff-only origin main` | Same | Fast-forward only; divergence requires review, not forced reset |
| Feature branch | `git switch -c feature/my-change` | Same | New development branch |
| Check Java | `java -version` | Same | JDK 17; wrong version: correct `JAVA_HOME`/PATH |
| Check SDK (tools on PATH) | `sdkmanager --list_installed` | `sdkmanager.bat --list_installed` | Lists Android 35/35.0.0; executable missing: add actual command-line tools `bin` to PATH |
| Install SDK | `sdkmanager 'platforms;android-35' 'build-tools;35.0.0' 'platform-tools'` | `sdkmanager.bat 'platforms;android-35' 'build-tools;35.0.0' 'platform-tools'` | Packages installed; accept licenses using `--licenses` first |
| Wrapper version | `./gradlew --version` | `.\gradlew.bat --version` | Gradle 8.9; missing wrapper JAR means incomplete source checkout |
| Available tasks | `./gradlew tasks --all` | `.\gradlew.bat tasks --all` | Task listing; SDK discovery/configuration must succeed |
| Debug APK | `./gradlew assembleDebug` | `.\gradlew.bat assembleDebug` | `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` |
| Debug tests | `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` | `.\gradlew.bat testDebugUnitTest` | Executed test report; failed assertions are not successful validation |
| Debug lint | `./gradlew lintDebug` | `.\gradlew.bat lintDebug` | `app/build/reports/lint-results-debug.html` |
| Release tests/lint/build | `./gradlew testReleaseUnitTest lintRelease assembleRelease` | `.\gradlew.bat testReleaseUnitTest lintRelease assembleRelease` | Signed `app-release.apk` only with valid original credentials; otherwise unsigned output is not production-ready |
| Clean generated outputs | `./gradlew clean` | `.\gradlew.bat clean` | Deletes build outputs; next build must regenerate them |
| Find APKs | `find app/build/outputs/apk -name '*.apk' -print` | `Get-ChildItem app\build\outputs\apk -Recurse -Filter *.apk` | Actual artifact paths; no output means no APK exists |
| Check debug package | `"$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/35.0.0/aapt" dump badging app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` | `& "$env:ANDROID_HOME\build-tools\35.0.0\aapt.exe" dump badging .\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk` | `com.electrokit.app`, version 3.0/code 14 |
| Verify debug signature | `"$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/35.0.0/apksigner" verify --verbose --print-certs app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk` | `& "$env:ANDROID_HOME\build-tools\35.0.0\apksigner.bat" verify --verbose --print-certs .\app\build\outputs\apk\debug\app-debug.apk` | Valid development certificate; compare original certificate separately for release updates |
| Check whitespace | `git diff --check` | Same | Empty output on success |
| Stage intentional files | `git add app docs scripts .github README.md CHANGELOG.md` | Same | Index contains reviewed changes; inspect `git diff --cached` |
| Commit | `git commit -m 'Describe the verified change'` | Same | New local commit; does not push or release |
| Push branch | `git push -u origin feature/my-change` | Same | Remote feature branch; requires write permission |
| Open PR (GitHub CLI authenticated) | `gh pr create --base main --head feature/my-change --title 'Describe change' --body-file /tmp/electro-pr.md` | `gh pr create --base main --head feature/my-change --title 'Describe change' --body-file "$env:TEMP\electro-pr.md"` | PR link; first write the reviewed description file. Git authentication alone does not establish GitHub API access |
| Release tag (after review) | `git tag -a v3.0 -m 'ELECTRO 3.0'` then `git push origin v3.0` | Same | Triggers signed-release workflow; do not run as an ordinary test |
| Publish verified signed file manually | `gh release create v3.0 app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk --verify-tag --title 'ELECTRO 3.0' --generate-notes` | Same paths may use backslashes | Public release, requiring reviewed tag, verified original signature and GitHub API write access |

Version editing is a source change: update `versionCode` and `versionName` in `app/build.gradle.kts`, review the diff, update changelog and rebuild. Do not blindly replace every version string across dependencies/history.

## Python tooling

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -r scripts/requirements-dev.txt
python scripts/check_comments.py
python -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'
python scripts/validate_assets.py
python scripts/validate_engineering.py
python scripts/validate_library.py
python scripts/check_contrast.py
python scripts/package_project.py --check
```

PowerShell: `python -m venv .venv`, then `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1`; other Python commands are unchanged. Each validator prints PASS only after checking its actual dataset. Intentional source changes require `python scripts/package_project.py` before `--check`; intentional palette changes require `python scripts/check_contrast.py --write`. Do not regenerate evidence to conceal a failing assertion or downloaded-artifact mismatch.

## Cloud-specific troubleshooting

Use `source /workspace/toolchains/activate-electro.sh` before Gradle and prepend `/workspace/toolchains/python-dev/bin` to PATH for Python tools. `JAVA_HOME`, `ANDROID_HOME`, `ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`, `ANDROID_USER_HOME`, `GRADLE_USER_HOME` and Java's `user.home` target writable workspace directories. The latter prevents Robolectric's download lock from targeting read-only `/home/agent`. Java uses the existing HTTPS proxy and system Java trust store; verification remains enabled.

An SDK cache manifest failure can be a writable-directory problem, not a missing package. A proxy 403 is access-policy evidence; do not disable TLS or substitute unverified downloads. Preserve underlying exit codes when logging (`> file 2>&1`, or Bash `set -o pipefail` before `tee`). Local setup helpers are outside the Git checkout. No worktree is needed for an already isolated cloud task.
````

## docs/DEVELOPMENT_GUIDE.md

````markdown
# Editing ELECTRO

Kotlin paths below start at `app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/`.

| Change | Actual owner and procedure |
|---|---|
| App name | `res/values/strings.xml` (`app_name`) and the visible brand in `ui/screens/WorkbenchScreen.kt`; keep applicationId for compatible updates |
| Launcher icon | `res/drawable/ic_launcher.xml`, `ic_launcher_monochrome.xml`, and `res/mipmap-anydpi*/ic_launcher.xml` wrappers |
| Home/navigation | `ui/screens/WorkbenchScreen.kt`, `MainScreen`; retain original route ownership in `ui/screens/App.kt` |
| Theme | `ui/theme/Theme.kt`; run `python scripts/check_contrast.py --write` and review light/dark/large-text previews |
| Legacy calculator | `domain/Calculators.kt`, `assets/registry.json` and `ui/screens/CalculatorScreen.kt`; retain old IDs |
| New utility | Add metadata and model to `domain/WorkbenchTools.kt`; `UtilityScreen.kt` supplies input, calculate/reset/save/copy controls |
| Formula | Modify domain code, state units and assumptions, add independent numeric and invalid-domain tests |
| Component image | Add descriptive PNG to `app/src/main/assets/components/` and an `id/name/category/image` entry to `components.json`; reuse identical assets |
| Connection drawing | Extend `ui/components/` or original `assets/pages.json`; specify connector variant, contact-number view and original source |
| Learning content | `data/ComponentLibrary.kt`; add citations and explicit limits. Meter illustration: `ui/components/MultimeterLesson.kt` |
| Fault records | `assets/engineering.json`; preserve original serial/code/message/reset/group fields unless an authoritative correction is supplied |
| Language | Extract new workbench Kotlin text into `res/values/strings.xml`, then add translated resource directories. Only English is currently implemented |
| Version | `app/build.gradle.kts`, `versionCode`/`versionName`; increase code monotonically |

For example, a new transformer-like utility needs explicit fields/units, a formula and limitations in `WorkbenchTools.all`, a calculation branch in `calculate`, and independent tests in `app/src/test/java/com/electrokit/app/domain/`. Do not duplicate a new database or replace an original calculator merely to restyle it.

Document APIs with meaningful KDoc and run the syntax-tree gate. Add regression coverage before fixing a confirmed bug. Preserve datastore identity, filenames, preference keys and route IDs unless implementing a tested migration.

After intentional edits run `python scripts/package_project.py`, then `--check`. Git internals, virtual environments, generated builds and private keys must stay out of source listings. Binary image bytes are covered by hashes without Base64 duplication in the listing.

Use a feature branch and review `git diff --check`, tests and APK metadata before committing. Never replace the production signing key with a newly generated development key.
````

## docs/GITHUB_RELEASE_GUIDE.md

````markdown
# Releases and signing

Android CI validates pull requests, main updates and manual runs, and uploads a **debug** APK plus diagnostic reports. These are development artifacts.

Release automation runs manually or on `v*` tags and requires repository Actions secrets:

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ELECTROKIT_KEYSTORE_BASE64` | Base64 of the original private signing keystore |
| `ELECTROKIT_STORE_PASSWORD` | Original keystore password |
| `ELECTROKIT_KEY_ALIAS` | Signing alias |
| `ELECTROKIT_KEY_PASSWORD` | Private key password |

Enter values through GitHub Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. The workflow decodes the key only into the runner's temporary directory, passes its path as `ELECTROKIT_KEYSTORE`, builds/tests/lints release and verifies the signed APK. Missing secrets fail explicitly. No unsigned APK is published as production-ready. GitHub's scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` supplies release permission; no personal token belongs in source.

Manual runs upload a signed artifact without creating a public Release. A version tag can publish `app-release.apk` after successful validation. The tag must match `defaultConfig.versionName`. Review code, CI and update compatibility before pushing a release tag.

From the repository root with secure signing variables already configured:

```bash
./gradlew testReleaseUnitTest lintRelease assembleRelease
"$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/35.0.0/apksigner" verify --verbose --print-certs app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
"$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/35.0.0/aapt" dump badging app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release.apk
```

PowerShell uses `.\gradlew.bat` and `& "$env:ANDROID_HOME\build-tools\35.0.0\apksigner.bat" ...`. The underlying app can produce an unsigned release without credentials; do not distribute it as signed production output.

After approving the exact release commit:

```bash
git tag -a v3.0 -m 'ELECTRO 3.0'
git push origin v3.0
```

These Git commands also work in PowerShell. Tags trigger release automation and are not ordinary test steps. This task does not imply a tag or GitHub Release has been published.

````

````markdown
# ELECTRO 3.0 release preparation

Application name: **ELECTRO**. Version name: **3.0**. Version code: **14**. Application ID remains `com.electrokit.app`.

The local optimized, non-debuggable release build passed `testReleaseUnitTest lintRelease assembleRelease`: **80 tests, 0 failures/errors/skips**, and no lint errors. R8 code/resource shrinking completed. Android SDK metadata confirms the requested name/version and SDK 24/35 bounds. Current output is `app/build/outputs/apk/release/app-release-unsigned.apk`; it is **unsigned**, not an installable production release.

The user selected the original signing identity. No replacement key has been generated. The original public certificate record in `verification/apk-signature.txt` has SHA-256:

`68a284d34b73344e4797a09137c06d330797f33a2c9d288580ae2749aa58bbaa`

No original keystore or signing-password variables are configured in this workspace. GitHub denied access to repository signing-secret metadata. The release workflow can check/use original secrets in GitHub without disclosing the private key locally, and it now rejects any signed APK whose certificate differs from this original record.

Required repository Actions secrets: `ELECTROKIT_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `ELECTROKIT_STORE_PASSWORD`, `ELECTROKIT_KEY_ALIAS`, `ELECTROKIT_KEY_PASSWORD`. Configure the **original** values securely under repository Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions. Never paste passwords into chat or commit a keystore. A certificate fingerprint or an old APK cannot recreate its private signing key.

The previous hosted release run failed inside the third-party Android setup action before signing. Workflows now pin Ubuntu 24.04 and use its documented preinstalled SDK, with explicit required-package checks. Signing prerequisites are checked early to avoid an expensive build when credentials are absent. Hosted execution is reported separately from successful local compilation.

When signed verification succeeds, the workflow packages `ELECTRO-3.0.apk` and the matching `ELECTRO-3.0-source.zip`. Manual execution uploads artifacts; a matching `v3.0` tag publishes both. Do not create the final release tag until the original signing identity has been verified.

The earlier `docs/BUILD_REPORT.md` records the 2.1.0 baseline's 120 debug/JVM/Robolectric tests; these are historical results, not a new 3.0 debug run. Device installation, production upgrade behavior and TalkBack remain unrun. See the audit report for existing engineering-content limitations.
````

## docs/UPDATE_GUIDE.md

````markdown
# Updating ELECTRO

1. Fetch current source, preserve local changes and create a feature branch.
2. Modify the owning source/data files and add regression coverage.
3. Increase `versionCode` and update `versionName` in `app/build.gradle.kts`; current version is 3.0/code 14.
4. Update `CHANGELOG.md`, including migration implications.
5. Run Python validators and Android tests/lint/debug build. Inspect actual APK metadata and reports.
6. Regenerate packaging/checksums and commit complete directories, including the wrapper JAR/catalog.
7. Open/review a pull request and require successful CI before merge.
8. Configure the original release keystore securely; build/test/lint release and verify with `apksigner`.
9. Check application ID, increasing versionCode and original signing certificate. Test an upgrade over the prior release with representative saved data.
10. Tag the reviewed commit, publish only the verified signed APK, download it and install over the compatible existing app.

Data continuity requires `com.electrokit.app`, a compatible original signing certificate and stable datastore/journal keys. A version name alone does not establish compatibility. Debug keys generally cannot update release-signed installations. The original 1.0.0 debug certificate may also differ.

Do not uninstall a valued installation just to bypass a certificate mismatch: uninstalling clears private data. Retain secure backups of the original key. No original release key was supplied in this task, so production signing and real upgrade compatibility remain untested.
````

## documentation/ENGINEERING_REQUIREMENTS.md

````markdown
# MASTER DEVELOPMENT PROMPT — ELECTRO APP

## 1. Role and Project Objective

Act as a senior Android developer, electrical and electronics R&D engineer, escalator control-system specialist, technical documentation engineer, and professional UI/UX designer.

I have an existing Android application called **ElectroKit**. Upgrade this existing project and rename the app to **Electro**.

The main objective is to build a professional, technically accurate, visually attractive, comprehensive electrical and electronics engineering application with a dedicated **Elevator & Escalator Engineering** module.

I have provided:

1. The existing ElectroKit Android project/source code.
2. Fourteen photographs containing handwritten escalator electrical, mechanical, PLC/MPC, control-panel, sensor, safety and motor engineering information.
3. A complete fault-code database containing 125 records.
4. Existing engineering calculators and application features that must remain operational.

**Do not rebuild the application as an unrelated project. Improve the existing codebase, retaining its calculations, settings, features, and architecture wherever practical.**

The development work must include complete implementation, testing, bug fixing, Android build verification, and professional technical illustrations.

## 11. Technical Accuracy and Safety

This application is an engineering reference, not a certified escalator safety controller.

Follow these requirements:

1. Never invent electrical ratings, component positions, terminal assignments, wiring connections or controller logic.
2. Cross-check handwritten information and identify uncertain readings.
3. Maintain a source and verification status for important records.
4. Do not recommend bypassing, bridging or disabling safety switches.
5. Do not give instructions to defeat overspeed protection, brake interlocks or safety controllers.
6. Clearly distinguish normal troubleshooting from safety-critical commissioning procedures.
7. Use applicable safety standards and manufacturer documentation only when verified and relevant.
8. Clearly indicate the difference between generic engineering information and equipment-specific Johnson-related reference material.
9. Do not claim that the application or its diagrams are OEM-approved unless approval is documented.
10. Treat manual reset, auto reset, alarm and warning classifications exactly as the supplied dataset records them.
````

````markdown
## 4905.jpg — Escalator terminology — page 1

SHA-256: `3fb199c123625b6cff8d38b79063b6d2fe9595b6bd0a564f0f7715fb6f19a808`

Duty cycle: typical daily usage of the escalator. Vertical rise H: floor-level difference at the escalator landings. Incline: angle of the inclined truss section relative to horizontal. Step width A: nominal tread width between skirts. Step-band speed: travelling speed of steps. Theoretical capacity: number of persons theoretically carried in one hour.
Drive station D: drive unit comprises electric motor, service brake, gearbox, and drive wheels for step chain and handrails. Tensioning/return station R: at bottom, where step-chain adjustment is made. Riser height: vertical height difference between adjacent steps. Truss supports S: support at each end with framing/chain reverting angles behind it on the building support beams (middle handwriting crowded).
Handrail clearance: clearance between sidewall and handrail. Pit P: area accommodating the horizontal truss portion. Inclination: passenger travel angle with respect to horizontal.
No numerical clearance or approved dimensional values are recorded.

## 4906.jpg — Escalator terminology — page 2

SHA-256: `c04dbbd93405c18f2d1c000b151efb86ad3eef2e7e9db15f36eef3e26bea9179`

Anti-slide device: on decking between adjacent handrails or at a wall to discourage sliding. Balustrade: enclosure alongside the running steps, comprising decking, inner/outer panels and skirts. Ceiling-intersection guard: guard at the escalator decking/building intersection. Comb: projecting part of the comb plate engaging tread grooves. Comb plate: landing plate supporting combs. Control equipment: controls motion, travel direction, speed and stopping.
Deck/decking extension: balustrade outside the moving handrail, transversely horizontal, including anti-slide devices where applicable. Driving machinery: mechanised power unit driving the escalator. Electromechanical brake: friction shoes on a drum or disc, spring applied and electrically released (one word partly crossed out). Handrail: powered moving rail for passengers to grip. Handrail guard: guard where handrail enters/leaves the balustrade.
These are educational definitions, not approved clearance values or a brake-design specification.

## 4907.jpg — Escalator terminology — page 3

SHA-256: `50075b56fb2f7c4985e9c3b1dba24632ec144a98aabe2b596384a80fee97b121`

Landing: stationary area at entrance/exit. Landing/floor plate: floor-plate portion next to comb plate on the landing; corrected handwriting partly crossed out. Newel: balustrade at the landing where moving handrail changes direction. Number of horizontal/flat steps: measured from the point the first step emerges from the comb plate to the first exposure of the riser of an adjacent step at both landings.
Panel: balustrade portion next to moving stairway occupying vertical space between steps and deck/inner panel. Skirt: immediately adjacent balustrade portion, between steps and deck/inner panel. Step: unit forming the moving stairway. Step chain: main chain to which steps are attached. Step-roller track: track carrying step rollers. Step tread: horizontal grooved part on which passengers stand. Step roller: roller supporting a step. Truss: supporting structure on which components are mounted. Warning band: demarcation of the step nose at floor-plate level. Contact length: horizontal distance between escalator landing point and end of escalator support.
Contact-length endpoints and the panel/skirt wording require the relevant dimensional drawing for precise interpretation.

## 4908.jpg — Annotated cutaway and step sketch

SHA-256: `567593091b10b513d892fc10dc7b8abd8446cdd7b1fd7e2aedcbf0aeff029a90`

Upper drive-station area: control panel, drive unit, upper sprocket, transformer, emergency brake, auxiliary brake, drive chain, main motor, gearbox/driving machine; top and bottom landing/step path; lower sprocket. Handrail, newel, balustrade, decking, sidewall, moving handrail, step rollers and operating pad are labelled.
Safety/device annotations: top LH/RH comb switches, handrail-inlet switches, comb vertical switch, top/middle/bottom skirt switches, step-upthrust, step-sag, top/middle stops, handrail-speed sensor, top radar sensor, bottom radar sensor, floor switches, step-chain switch, handrail-broken switch, handrail guard/entry. Some fine arrows overlap; exact switch mounting coordinates and some LH/RH annotations are uncertain.
Step detail: step tread, cleat, step demarcation line, riser, step chain, and trailing roller/drive-roller wording (roller terminology ambiguous). One “8…” annotation near the lower handrail entry is not legible; no dimension is recovered.
This drawing supports approximate educational locations only, not installation coordinates or a wiring diagram.
````
