# Electro 2.0.1 — response to Electro_Audit_Report.pdf

This report distinguishes source fixes from physical-device validation. The supplied five-field fault dataset, reference IDs, application ID and signing identity are preserved. No OEM diagnostic cause, location, connection or rating was invented to fill content gaps.

## Issue status

| ID | Outcome |
|---|---|
| H1 | Fixed: explicit primary/secondary/tertiary, container/on-container, error, inverse, outline and elevation roles replace Material baseline purple. Dark and light use the same green identity. |
| H2 | Fixed: five equal-width tabs use shorter labels, no horizontal discovery requirement and custom content without Material's clipping text inset. Labels can wrap at large fonts. Existing pager and route order are retained. Added visible-tab regression coverage. |
| H3 | Fixed: API24 fallback and adaptive launcher use identical E/energy artwork. Adaptive foreground is transparent and its content stays within the central safe area. Its base is provided by icon_background. |
| H4 | Fixed in presentation: remove repeated description/possible-causes cards; show one explicit source/diagnostic-limit note. Exact original fault label and classifications remain. Generic legacy explanation fields remain in JSON for backwards compatibility, and repeated safety context on standalone component pages has not been comprehensively rewritten. This release does not claim new fault-specific OEM diagnoses. |
| M1 | Fixed: XML status bar and Activity edge-to-edge status colour match the toolbar green. |
| M2 | Improved: neutral brand starting window; committed DataStore theme mirrored into a small local launch hint; Activity uses that hint before the asynchronous load and adjusts navigation-bar contrast. DataStore remains authoritative; reset clears the hint. Light save/recreation is covered in Robolectric. Installations without a hint use the neutral brand window/loading surface until DataStore loads, rather than choosing an unconfirmed dark/light canvas. No physical cold-start video was recorded. |
| M3 | Fixed: darker light-mode primary. Source-derived checks now cover primary text on both tinted surfaces and four semantic container/on-container pairs in both palettes. Every tested pair exceeds 4.5:1. |
| M4 | Fixed: red identification cells use #C62828 and luminance-selected contrasting text. |
| M5 | Fixed for surrounding cards: drawing backplates follow the current surfaceContainerHigh. Metal/insulator/wire artwork retains its own material colours so identification is not lost in dark mode. |
| M6 | Fixed in global search: shared registry content is deduplicated by contentId. Intentional cross-tab aliases remain available in both reference lists. |
| M7 | Fixed visible navigation: Data tab/action and database-cylinder icon replace the puzzle metaphor. The database screen retains its explanatory Databases title. Legacy PLUGINS keys/function/resource identifiers remain internal compatibility details. |
| M8 | Fixed active duplicates through string-resource aliases; unused description/possible-cause and removed row-subtitle labels were deleted. |
| M9 | Extended: pink, clear, colon-qualified colour descriptions and two-colour slash values. Slash colours receive adjacent swatches with the label on the normal theme surface, rather than text across two conflicting backgrounds. Unknown textual values remain uncoloured. |
| Hardcoded colours | Partially consolidated: eleven near-duplicate light metal tones share DrawingMetal; surrounding card colours use semantic theme tokens. Physical material, wire and schematic identification colours remain explicit. A complete conversion of all artwork colours to named material tokens was not performed. |
| L1 | Fixed: Fibre optic cable colour consistently uses British spelling in registry and page title. |
| L2 | Improved: Info and Share page/Share results use normal casing. Small Data toolbar label remains intentionally compact. |
| L3 | Fixed reference page title alignment to start. Technical drawing labels retain their individual placement. |
| L4 | Fixed table/header horizontal padding from 12dp to the same 16dp section margin. Complete caption/button alignment across every specialised diagram has not been independently audited. |

| L6 | Fixed: removed the repeated home-row subtitle. Titles and individual component icons remain. |
| L7 | Fixed: USB header retains Mini/Micro in full. |
| L8 | Fixed chip wrapping by keeping each filter group in one horizontal scroll row. The one-record Alarm group is preserved because it is authoritative source data. |
| L9 | Improved: larger numbered cutaway markers and selection radius. Accessible legend buttons remain the reliable 48dp+ selection alternative; small inline markers are not claimed to be standalone 48dp targets. Zoom/pan remain available. |
| L10 | Not a required compatibility upgrade: pinned dependencies remain. Lint warnings are reported below rather than suppressed or described as fixed. Dependency migration requires its own SDK/API compatibility verification. |

The first-upgrade launch uses neutral brand colour until DataStore loads; actual on-device transition timing remains unmeasured.

Only 9 of 72 legacy reference pages have external citation URLs; the other pages retain their provenance/verification limitations. Adding invented links would not verify the data. Ambiguous photograph identifiers and OEM-specific fault trigger logic remain explicitly unverified. No certified machine-control capability or live CBM interface is claimed.

# ElectroKit 1.1.0 revision 2 — implementation response

This records source changes and executed checks, not independent certification. Exact command outcomes belong to FIX_REPORT.md, VALIDATION.md and verification/.

| IDs | Implemented scope |
| --- | --- |
| A1–A4 | KDoc covers Kotlin types, callables (including local helpers), class/file properties and constructor fields. Repository schema fields, theme roles, calculator dispatch formulas, parser grammar, rounding promotion, CVD coefficients, IPC constants, debounce snapshots and corruption handling are explained. Build sections, workflow and Python functions carry comments. |
| A5–A6 | The syntax-tree checker rejects missing KDoc and function parameter/return tags and enforces the requested five-file 1:8 density floor. Temporary local vals/lambda parameters are excluded. Syntax errors fail coverage rather than silently lowering the declaration count. CI runs the gate using pinned developer-only parser dependencies. This checks structure, not prose quality. |
| B1 | Decimal/percent display uses four significant digits and trims fractional zeros. Fractional band tolerances remain exact. ADC integer displays use an unrounded path. |
| B2 | RTD inverse bisection quantises to 1e-6 °C and normalises signed zero. Default output is `Temperature: 0 °C`; sensor uncertainty is unchanged. |
| B3 | Unitless and V/V quantities use six-significant-digit decimal/scientific notation without SI prefix letters. |
| B4 | R notation uses BigDecimal plain strings. Values exceeding the stated practical string-length limit receive an explicit message. Numeric/EIA-96 alternatives remain labelled approximations. |
| B5 | Retry retains the failed load/settings/input/reset action. Injectable AppRepository permits ViewModel failure tests that distinguish a settings mutation from an unrelated empty input flush. Cancellation is preserved. |
| B6–B7 | Meg/MEG aliases restored. Negative suffix powers use division; `10u` and `10uF` exactly equal the Double literal `1e-5`. General floating-point arithmetic still has rounding limits. |
| C1–C3 | Controls, help/accessibility text, storage errors and product prose use Android resources. Composable code uses stringResource; share/ViewModel code uses Context resources. English domain labels/formulas/validation are centralised in Messages. Technical symbols and offline reference/module JSON remain English; full localisation is not claimed. Changes presents product improvements instead of “Audit fixes”. |
| D1 | Contrast checks parse actual palette/toolbar hex tokens, require 4.5:1 for five text pairs, and reject a stale contrast.txt. This does not certify every overlay or colour swatch. |
| D2–D3 | README describes the current revision once. Historical notes moved to CHANGELOG. The listing, tree and checksums are regenerated using the committed generator. This replaces the previous broad documentation claim. |
| E | Existing tests retained. Added tests cover rounding, RTD zero, unitless text, small SMD values, aliases/exact micro parsing, settings/input retry targeting, and positive/negative quality-gate fixtures. The retained per-field extreme grid adds abc/NaN to its previous samples. |

Earlier ratio bounds, suffix precedence, fractional tolerances, explicit numeric metadata, asynchronous loading, atomic DataStore updates and optimised release settings remain. An OS kill during debounce can still lose the final unsaved keystroke. Legitimate empty reference cells remain; unspecified wire colours are not invented. The release certificate is retained and private signing material is excluded from source.

Only **9 of 72** shared reference pages have source URLs. Per-cell/table traceability, additional connector variants, broader PIC memory/peripheral fields and licensed standards review remain incomplete. PIC10F320/322 remain standard Mid-range. No new certification of reference accuracy is claimed.

No physical device or emulator was used. API-34 Robolectric simulations do not execute the obfuscated release on a device. TalkBack speech, manufacturer-specific startup behaviour, actual airplane-mode operation and real-device release behaviour remain unverified. No lint baseline or suppression was added to hide failures.

UnitCatalog covers the declared compound units and metre context; already-scaled display units no longer receive another prefix. Provenance is disclosed on all 72 pages, but external citation coverage is still 9/72. No real-device/emulator pass is claimed. Current measured outcomes belong to VALIDATION.md and verification/summary.json.

adb install -r ElectroKit-1.1.2.apk
adb shell am force-stop com.electrokit.app
adb shell monkey -p com.electrokit.app 1

| Airplane mode | All calculator/reference/database routes work without connectivity | Not run |
| Clipboard/share chooser | Copied text and shared units/results are correct | Not run |

| A3 | Explains numeric grammar, suffix precedence, rounding promotion, negative-scale division, CVD coefficients, IPC constants, debounce/pending ownership and corruption preservation. | domain/Engineering.kt; viewmodel/AppViewModel.kt; data/PreferenceCodec.kt |

| A5 | Five requested files meet at least one comment line per eight nonblank code lines. The coverage report records measured counts, not a hand-maintained estimate. | Calculators.kt; Engineering.kt; App.kt; CalculatorScreen.kt; AppViewModel.kt; verification/comments.txt |
| A6 | Syntax-tree KDoc gate, parameter/return-tag checks, syntax-error failure, density gate and negative/positive fixtures; runs in CI. Temporary local vals and lambda parameters are outside the API-declaration gate. | scripts/check_comments.py; scripts/requirements-dev.txt; scripts/test_quality_checks.py; android.yml |

Non-composable owners resolve Context resources. | strings.xml; App.kt; CalculatorScreen.kt; Drawings.kt; AppViewModel.kt; domain/Messages.kt; domain calculators/parser/filter |

Extends the existing per-field extreme grid with abc/NaN without removing its original samples. | FormattingRegressionTests.kt; RetryRegressionTests.kt; AuditRegressionTests.kt; test_quality_checks.py |

API-declaration coverage does not imply that every temporary variable has KDoc, nor can a parser grade comment quality. English technical symbols and bundled reference/module datasets are not a complete localisation system.

The per-field grid evaluates every declared calculator field in every supported mode with empty text, garbage, abc, NaN, -1, 0, 1e-300 and 1e300. Its measured case total is printed in the JUnit XML. ## documentation/history/IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md

````markdown
# Electro 2.0.0 implementation and verification report

This release upgrades the existing ElectroKit project; it is not an unrelated replacement. The display name/icon are Electro, while com.electrokit.app, existing packages/preferences, input journal and release signing certificate remain compatible.

## Implemented requirements

1. Renamed launcher/toolbar/Info/Changes branding and supplied original vector icon; internal stable identifiers retained.
2. Preserved all 31 original calculators, 55 pin-outs, 21 resources, three always-available databases, saved settings and footer-free personal-use behaviour.
3. Added the twelve requested engineering sections plus dedicated CBM navigation and local global search across engineering text, sources, identifiers, faults, tools and legacy catalogue titles.
4. Imported all 125 supplied fault records exactly; separate golden TSV/JSON comparisons preserve serial gaps 112–114, string codes 164–168, messages, groups and reset types.
5. Added fault search, intersected group/reset/system/bookmark filters, detail pages, copy/share, related faults and bidirectional technical-topic links. Relationships are explicitly not approved wiring/trigger logic.
6. Visually inspected all fourteen photographs, rotating sideways pages for inspection; readable engineering content, source hashes, uncertain/cropped text and repeated notes are transcribed in the app and documentation.
7. Added 245 technical records covering mechanical definitions, component/device identification, safety switches, MPC I/O, separate additional X/Y notes, motor/brakes, conceptual sequences and CBM references.
8. Added original industrial figures and a source-grounded educational cutaway with fifteen selectable regions, accessible legend, enlarged view, zoom and pan. Logical terminal controls navigate to functions without asserting physical pin positions. Q9–Q12 remain grouped.
9. Added fifteen calculators with explicit input units, formulas/substitution steps, assumptions, examples loaded only on request, validation and durable saved values/copy/reset/share. Existing shared-unit parsing fixes remain; new dimensional checks do not change the legacy generic-parser API.
10. Added fixed, clearly simulated CBM values and selectable educational water/communication events with real links to supplied fault references. No live interface or fictitious protocol/register map is provided.
11. Retained KDoc/developer quality gates; added engineering source/graph validation to CI. The actual CI service was not run here.

## Executed results

- Committed-wrapper assembleDebug, assembleRelease, testDebugUnitTest, testReleaseUnitTest, lintDebug and lintRelease: PASS.
- 91 debug tests and 67 release JVM tests passed, zero failures/errors/skips. Debug includes actual Compose navigation/search/filter/bookmark/recreation/cutaway-dialog/terminal/calculator/CBM checks under Robolectric API 34.
- Existing 1,984-case extreme-input grid retained; 266 new per-field extreme probes cover all new tool schemas.
- Four Python quality tests and KDoc, legacy asset, engineering exact-import/graph, source-derived contrast and packaging gates: PASS.
- Release identity/label/min24/target35, non-debuggable status, v2/v3 signatures, unchanged certificate, no-INTERNET permission and packaged JSON/source byte equality: verified.
- Lint has zero errors; exact warning counts/IDs remain in verification/summary.json and raw reports. Warnings are not suppressed to suggest a warning-free build.

## Corrections made during development

- Preserved the legacy generic parser's optional-dimension contract after a regression test caught a stricter global change; strict dimensionless validation belongs only to new explicitly unitless fields.
- Fixed duplicate search/title semantics in new UI tests by targeting the intended noneditable result, rather than weakening the actual assertions.
- Made the longer system/location filter compact and kept explicit group/reset/bookmark controls accessible.
- Kept brake-liner wear references separate from unverified brake-position input mappings.
- Explicitly distinguished photograph/source authority, educational diagrams and simulated readings.

## Uncertainties and unexecuted work

TECHNICAL_VERIFICATION.md lists ambiguous handwriting, missing terminal specifications, the motor example's rounded-data inconsistency and absent ambient rating. No OEM-verified causes/thresholds, exact contactor timing, certified safety sequence, approved wiring/clearances or installation coordinates are invented. Live connectivity is deliberately absent because the required authorised interface/protocol/register map was not supplied.

No physical phone, API-24/recent emulator, TalkBack speech, real airplane-mode run or release/R8 execution on a device was performed. Robolectric rendering is not a substitute for those tests. Existing legacy external-citation coverage remains 9/72 pages. Manufacturer publications provide limited generic context, not approval of the supplied controller data.

## documentation/history/REVIEW_RESPONSE.md

````markdown
# Review response — 1.1.2

## Implemented

1. **Field units:** central UnitCatalog supplies parser units, declared-unit aliases and conversion factors. Compound m/s, oz/ft² and °C/W are supported. mA and kW already parsed via SI prefixes; explicit conversion tests now protect them. Metres were another ambiguity: 10m remains milli in bare engineering syntax, but means ten metres in a metre field. A regression iterates every numeric field in all 31 specifications. Already-scaled output labels also remain intact, preventing invalid stacked prefixes such as mmm or mmA.
2. **Pending input:** a small AtomicFile journal is written synchronously, fsynced and read back before acknowledging an input edit. DataStore commits immediately in the background; the deliberate 300 ms debounce is removed. Startup overlays/replays journal values and clears only snapshots whose main-record transaction completed. Newer edits cannot be cleared by an older acknowledgement. Corrupt backups surface an error. This trades a small synchronous private-file write per edit for stronger durability; storage failures or interruption before acknowledgement are not guaranteed.
3. **Provenance visibility:** all 72 pages now disclose their provenance/verification status before the table and include it in shared text. The asset gate rejects missing provenance. **External citation coverage remains 9/72.** The other 63 are explicitly marked unverified; no invented URLs or claim of standards verification was added. Full source attribution remains open.
4. **Lint:** tool, database-entry and part counts use Android plurals; unused developer credit string removed. Predictive-back opt-in is retained: it is intentional on recent Android versions, not a demonstrated API-24 crash. Android reference: https://developer.android.com/guide/navigation/custom-back/predictive-back-gesture. Dependency versions remain pinned to the tested API-35 toolchain; newer versions alone do not establish a product defect, and no untested dependency migration is claimed.

## Validation boundaries

No physical device/emulator was available in this environment, and no /dev/kvm acceleration is exposed. DEVICE_VALIDATION.md provides reproducible release-install/recovery checks with every device result marked Not run. TalkBack speech, actual airplane mode and on-device R8 behaviour remain unverified. Remote CI was not triggered here.

The project does not use pytest. Its Python quality tests run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts -p 'test_*.py'`, after installing scripts/requirements-dev.txt. A missing Android SDK is a build-host prerequisite failure, not independent evidence of a Kotlin compilation defect.

The personal-use behaviour is retained: no empty footer, all three databases always available, no Enable/Disable controls, no INTERNET permission. Release signing is retained for an in-place update.

Final measured outcomes are recorded in VALIDATION.md and verification/summary.json after the fresh build completes.

## Final measured results

- Wrapper build and both lint tasks: passed, zero lint errors.
- Debug tests: 68 passed; release JVM tests: 50 passed; zero failed/errors/skipped.
- Python unittest quality checks: four passed; KDoc, asset/provenance and contrast gates passed.
- APK signature, app identity, no-INTERNET property and packaged JSON/source equality: verified.
- External citations: still 9/72. Real-device/emulator checks: not run. Dependencies remain pinned; intentional predictive-back compatibility warning retained.

See verification/summary.json, raw reports, REFERENCE_COVERAGE.md and DEVICE_VALIDATION.md for the exact limits.

````

## documentation/history/TECHNICAL_VERIFICATION_2_0_0.md

````markdown
# Electro 2.0.0 technical-data verification

## Authority and exact import

All 125 supplied rows were imported as separate records. The five original fields are tested against a separate source TSV: serial, code string, exact message, reset type and group. Serial gaps 112–114 remain; numeric-looking codes 164–168 remain strings. No A/E records are merged. Derived browsing categories, explanations, possible causes and related-topic links are separate and explicitly not approved trigger/wiring logic.

All fourteen photographs were visually inspected. Sideways pages were rotated for inspection. Every readable technical topic, identifier list, motor parameter and labelled sketch region was transcribed, including repeated/cropped notes and blanks, with source filenames and SHA-256 hashes. The original photographs are not raster assets inside the APK. See documentation/PHOTO_TRANSCRIPTIONS.md and the in-app Technical Reference Library.

## Specific uncertainties preserved

- K14 and K03 are overwritten; typed schedule values are retained as supplied, not independently approved.
- Some identifiers on 4886(1).jpg are cropped; the typed schedule supplies their restored readings.
- The first handwritten I13 speed is difficult to read; typed 0.45/0.65 is retained without asserting a configured speed or permitted setting.
- I7 handwriting resembles “contactor stack”; supplied description Contactor Status is identified as the typed interpretation.
- I10/I11 have no supplied function. I15/I16 are marked reserved in the notes. No B07–B10 sensor assignments are inferred.
- Q9–Q12 remain one inverter-control group. No individual output function, voltage, contact type or common wiring is invented.
- S27 is overwritten; the drive-chain suffix in S21A needs confirmation. S22 is linked only as a brake topic: emergency/auxiliary terminology is not treated as proof of identical devices or logic.
- S05–S08 brake-liner wear references are kept distinct from I8/I9 brake-position/limit feedback. Their electrical equivalence is not asserted.
- B02 is written as sensor B in one image and sensor 2 in another. Both readings remain visible.
- EK05/EK15 traffic-light lettering may be EL05/EL15. These identifiers require drawing confirmation.
- Additional X/Y/OP/BIT/BM/RS485 notes have no confirmed controller model. BM and BIT handwriting and OP polarity notation are uncertain; X terminals are not equated with MPC I terminals.
- The motor serial appears 256/HE15-0202; manufacturer/IE3 lettering is not verified. Ambient-temperature value is absent. Recorded example weight is approximately 163 kg, not a universal motor weight.
- Motor V/I/PF imply 16.3886647 kW input and 91.5266755% efficiency at 15 kW shaft output, slightly different from the recorded 91.2%. At 975 rpm, shaft torque is 146.912255 N·m. If six poles are explicitly assumed, 50 Hz gives 1000 rpm synchronous speed and 2.5% slip. Pole count is not a photographed rating.
- Mechanical contact-length endpoints, panel/skirt wording, crowded truss-support wording, roller terminology and overlapping sketch arrows need the actual dimensional/OEM drawing. No unreadable “8…” annotation is recovered as a dimension.

## Engineering calculations

Independent numerical fixtures cover new power, current, efficiency, PF, torque, synchronous speed/slip, frequency/speed, gear speed/reverse ratio, kinematic capacity/step speed, geometry, energy and conversion results. Every scalar field is independently probed with empty, zero, negative, extremely small/large, NaN and malformed values. The pre-existing extreme-input grid remains.

New numerical fields start empty. Examples are explicit educational inputs; their geometry is not claimed to be an actual machine specification. Balanced sinusoidal power models, shaft-versus-input power, entered efficiency/slip, whole-number poles/teeth and the distinction between theoretical capacity and measured throughput are stated. Units are validated through the shared parser; existing generic-parser behaviour remains compatible, while new dimensionless fields reject pasted physical units.

## Diagrams and CBM

The cutaway and 15 markers are original educational artwork grounded in the supplied sketch's approximate functional regions. Marker coordinates are illustration coordinates, not millimetres or job mounting coordinates. The artwork is selectable and supports zoom/pan. Other equipment illustrations are identification aids, not manufacturer construction or wiring drawings. Logical terminal buttons never pretend to be a physical connector pinout.

CBM values and selectable water/communication scenarios are visibly SIMULATED. They do not reproduce the MPC's trigger logic or establish normal/trip thresholds. No live interface is implemented without an authorised protocol, register map and electrical-interface specification.

## Sources reviewed for general context

- ABB Technical Guide No. 7, induction motor fundamentals and nominal power/torque: https://library.e.abb.com/public/e555e5106a3c44e882f48b75a44f6807/Technical_guide_No_7_3AFE64362569_RevD_EN_lowres.pdf
- Schindler Planning Guide, planning/capacity context: https://www.schindler.lu/content/dam/website/lu/docs/schindler-escalators-planning-guide-en.pdf/_jcr_content/renditions/original./schindler-escalators-planning-guide-en.pdf

Reviewed 26 October 2026. These publications do not validate the supplied Johnson-related controller, fault thresholds, wiring or installed motor. The user photographs and supplied dataset retain their own authority. No numerical statutory clearance, certified stopping distance or switch-bypass procedure is supplied.

## Not verified / not claimed

No OEM approval, certified controller behaviour, exact contactor switching sequence, live machine connectivity, field-test qualification or installation compliance. No instructions to bypass, bridge, disable or defeat protective devices. No physical-device, TalkBack speech, real airplane-mode or API-24/recent-emulator run. Executed automated evidence belongs in VALIDATION.md and verification/, not a claim of field certification.

````

## documentation/history/VALIDATION.md

````markdown
# Electro 2.0.0 validation

The committed Gradle 8.9 wrapper ran with JDK 17, SDK/Build Tools 35 and the existing external signing key:

```sh
./gradlew assembleDebug assembleRelease testDebugUnitTest testReleaseUnitTest lintDebug lintRelease -Pkotlin.compiler.execution.strategy=in-process -Pkotlin.incremental=false
```

BUILD SUCCESSFUL. 91 debug tests and 67 release JVM tests passed, zero failures/errors/skips. Both lint tasks have zero errors; raw warnings are retained. Four Python quality tests, KDoc, original assets, exact engineering import/graph, contrast and packaging checks passed. The original 1,984 extreme cases plus 266 new per-field probes remain.

The signed R8-shrunk release is Electro 2.0.0/code9, com.electrokit.app, min24/target35, non-debuggable, v2/v3 signed with the unchanged release certificate. No INTERNET permission. Every packaged JSON asset matches source. AndroidX's app-private receiver signature permission remains; this does not mean the APK declares no permissions at all.

Actual Compose rendering/navigation ran under Robolectric API34, including new fault search/filter/bookmark/recreation, linked records, terminal selection, cutaway inspection controls, motor calculator and CBM scenarios. Preview PNGs are simulated Android screenshots, not physical-device screenshots. Device/API24-emulator/TalkBack/real-airplane-mode/release-on-phone and remote-CI execution were not performed. The existing device-environment preflight is retained as historical environment evidence, not a newly executed device test.

See verification/summary.json and raw test/lint/signature outputs, IMPLEMENTATION_REPORT.md and TECHNICAL_VERIFICATION.md for concrete results and limits.

````

## documentation/history/VISUAL_UPDATE.md

````markdown
# ElectroKit 1.2.0 — reference illustrations

This update addresses recognisability of hardware inside reference pages. All artwork is original Compose Canvas vector work; none of the supplied screenshots or another application's drawings/photos are embedded.

## Changes

- Distinct illustrations for D-sub ports, Centronics, circular housings, modular connectors, power housings, RCA, TRRS jack, Uno R3 board identification, DIP14 ICs and TO-220 regulators.
- Metal gradients, recessed contacts, gold finishes, moulded insulation, mounting hardware and board components replace repeated outline boxes on 28 reference diagrams.
- New hardware illustrations have an Enlarge diagram action opening a larger, scrollable inspection view with a Close action.
- USB drawings gain metallic surface shading and recessed inserts. Remaining logical contact maps gain shaded surfaces and gold contacts; specialised circuit, switch and logic symbols remain schematic.
- Colour-name cells use the actual colour across the cell, with black/white text selected by relative luminance. Text labels remain so colour is not the only cue.
- Personal-use behaviour is retained: no reserved footer, all databases immediately available, no enable/disable switches, no INTERNET permission.

## Technical limits

Housing illustrations of circular/power connectors are intentionally unnumbered: their previous JSON coordinates were logical index grids, not verified physical contact positions. Captions explicitly distinguish these illustrations from wiring guides. Tables preserve the original data. D-sub/Centronics drawings state the male mating-face view. The Uno is a simplified identification illustration, not a manufacturer photo or an exact PCB manufacturing drawing. No new technical source claims are made.

Not every connector has a bespoke mechanical drawing yet: USB and the newly illustrated families have specialised renderers; other pages still use improved logical contact maps. Existing external-citation and real-device validation gaps remain. Robolectric screenshots are simulated Android rendering, not photographs or device validation.

## Final measured results

- Wrapper build and both lint tasks: passed, zero lint errors.
- Debug tests: 69 passed; release JVM tests: 50 passed; zero failed/errors/skipped.
- Python unittest quality checks: four passed; KDoc, asset/provenance and contrast gates passed.
- APK signature, app identity, no-INTERNET property and packaged JSON/source equality: verified.
- External citations: still 9/72. Real-device/emulator checks: not run. Dependencies remain pinned; intentional predictive-back compatibility warning retained.

See verification/summary.json, raw reports, REFERENCE_COVERAGE.md and DEVICE_VALIDATION.md for the exact limits.

````

````text
#!/bin/sh

#
# Copyright © 2015-2021 the original authors.
#
# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
# You may obtain a copy of the License at
#
#      https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
#
# Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
# distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
# WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
# See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
# limitations under the License.
#
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
#

##############################################################################
#
#   Gradle start up script for POSIX generated by Gradle.
#
#   Important for running:
#
#   (1) You need a POSIX-compliant shell to run this script. If your /bin/sh is
#       noncompliant, but you have some other compliant shell such as ksh or
#       bash, then to run this script, type that shell name before the whole
#       command line, like:
#
#           ksh Gradle
#
#       Busybox and similar reduced shells will NOT work, because this script
#       requires all of these POSIX shell features:
#         * functions;
#         * expansions «$var», «${var}», «${var:-default}», «${var+SET}»,
#           «${var#prefix}», «${var%suffix}», and «$( cmd )»;
#         * compound commands having a testable exit status, especially «case»;
#         * various built-in commands including «command», «set», and «ulimit».
#
#   Important for patching:
#
#   (2) This script targets any POSIX shell, so it avoids extensions provided
#       by Bash, Ksh, etc; in particular arrays are avoided.
#
#       The "traditional" practice of packing multiple parameters into a
#       space-separated string is a well documented source of bugs and security
#       problems, so this is (mostly) avoided, by progressively accumulating
#       options in "$@", and eventually passing that to Java.
#
#       Where the inherited environment variables (DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS,
#       and GRADLE_OPTS) rely on word-splitting, this is performed explicitly;
#       see the in-line comments for details.
#
#       There are tweaks for specific operating systems such as AIX, CygWin,
#       Darwin, MinGW, and NonStop.
#
#   (3) This script is generated from the Groovy template
#       https://github.com/gradle/gradle/blob/HEAD/platforms/jvm/plugins-application/src/main/resources/org/gradle/api/internal/plugins/unixStartScript.txt
#       within the Gradle project.
#
#       You can find Gradle at https://github.com/gradle/gradle/.
#
##############################################################################

# Attempt to set APP_HOME

# Resolve links: $0 may be a link
app_path=$0

# Need this for daisy-chained symlinks.
while
    APP_HOME=${app_path%"${app_path##*/}"}  # leaves a trailing /; empty if no leading path
    [ -h "$app_path" ]
do
    ls=$( ls -ld "$app_path" )
    link=${ls#*' -> '}
    case $link in             #(
      /*)   app_path=$link ;; #(
      *)    app_path=$APP_HOME$link ;;
    esac
done

# This is normally unused
# shellcheck disable=SC2034
APP_BASE_NAME=${0##*/}
# Discard cd standard output in case $CDPATH is set (https://github.com/gradle/gradle/issues/25036)
APP_HOME=$( cd -P "${APP_HOME:-./}" > /dev/null && printf '%s
' "$PWD" ) || exit

# Use the maximum available, or set MAX_FD != -1 to use that value.
MAX_FD=maximum

warn () {
    echo "$*"
} >&2

die () {
    echo
    echo "$*"
    echo
    exit 1
} >&2

# OS specific support (must be 'true' or 'false').
cygwin=false
msys=false
darwin=false
nonstop=false
case "$( uname )" in                #(
  CYGWIN* )         cygwin=true  ;; #(
  Darwin* )         darwin=true  ;; #(
  MSYS* | MINGW* )  msys=true    ;; #(
  NONSTOP* )        nonstop=true ;;
esac

CLASSPATH=$APP_HOME/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.jar


# Determine the Java command to use to start the JVM.
if [ -n "$JAVA_HOME" ] ; then
    if [ -x "$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java" ] ; then
        # IBM's JDK on AIX uses strange locations for the executables
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/jre/sh/java
    else
        JAVACMD=$JAVA_HOME/bin/java
    fi
    if [ ! -x "$JAVACMD" ] ; then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: $JAVA_HOME

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
else
    JAVACMD=java
    if ! command -v java >/dev/null 2>&1
    then
        die "ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH.

Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the
location of your Java installation."
    fi
fi

# Increase the maximum file descriptors if we can.
if ! "$cygwin" && ! "$darwin" && ! "$nonstop" ; then
    case $MAX_FD in #(
      max*)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -H is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        MAX_FD=$( ulimit -H -n ) ||
            warn "Could not query maximum file descriptor limit"
    esac
    case $MAX_FD in  #(
      '' | soft) :;; #(
      *)
        # In POSIX sh, ulimit -n is undefined. That's why the result is checked to see if it worked.
        # shellcheck disable=SC2039,SC3045
        ulimit -n "$MAX_FD" ||
            warn "Could not set maximum file descriptor limit to $MAX_FD"
    esac
fi

# Collect all arguments for the java command, stacking in reverse order:
#   * args from the command line
#   * the main class name
#   * -classpath
#   * -D...appname settings
#   * --module-path (only if needed)
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and GRADLE_OPTS environment variables.

# For Cygwin or MSYS, switch paths to Windows format before running java
if "$cygwin" || "$msys" ; then
    APP_HOME=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$APP_HOME" )
    CLASSPATH=$( cygpath --path --mixed "$CLASSPATH" )

    JAVACMD=$( cygpath --unix "$JAVACMD" )

    # Now convert the arguments - kludge to limit ourselves to /bin/sh
    for arg do
        if
            case $arg in                                #(
              -*)   false ;;                            # don't mess with options #(
              /?*)  t=${arg#/} t=/${t%%/*}              # looks like a POSIX filepath
                    [ -e "$t" ] ;;                      #(
              *)    false ;;
            esac
        then
            arg=$( cygpath --path --ignore --mixed "$arg" )
        fi
        # Roll the args list around exactly as many times as the number of
        # args, so each arg winds up back in the position where it started, but
        # possibly modified.
        #
        # NB: a `for` loop captures its iteration list before it begins, so
        # changing the positional parameters here affects neither the number of
        # iterations, nor the values presented in `arg`.
        shift                   # remove old arg
        set -- "$@" "$arg"      # push replacement arg
    done
fi


# Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS='"-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"'

# Collect all arguments for the java command:
#   * DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, JAVA_OPTS, and optsEnvironmentVar are not allowed to contain shell fragments,
#     and any embedded shellness will be escaped.
#   * For example: A user cannot expect ${Hostname} to be expanded, as it is an environment variable and will be
#     treated as '${Hostname}' itself on the command line.

set -- \
        "-Dorg.gradle.appname=$APP_BASE_NAME" \
        -classpath "$CLASSPATH" \
        org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain \
        "$@"

# Stop when "xargs" is not available.
if ! command -v xargs >/dev/null 2>&1
then
    die "xargs is not available"
fi

# Use "xargs" to parse quoted args.
#
# With -n1 it outputs one arg per line, with the quotes and backslashes removed.
#
# In Bash we could simply go:
#
#   readarray ARGS < <( xargs -n1 <<<"$var" ) &&
#   set -- "${ARGS[@]}" "$@"
#
# but POSIX shell has neither arrays nor command substitution, so instead we
# post-process each arg (as a line of input to sed) to backslash-escape any
# character that might be a shell metacharacter, then use eval to reverse
# that process (while maintaining the separation between arguments), and wrap
# the whole thing up as a single "set" statement.
#
# This will of course break if any of these variables contains a newline or
# an unmatched quote.
#

eval "set -- $(
        printf '%s\n' "$DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS $JAVA_OPTS $GRADLE_OPTS" |
        xargs -n1 |
        sed ' s~[^-[:alnum:]+,./:=@_]~\\&~g; ' |
        tr '\n' ' '
    )" '"$@"'

exec "$JAVACMD" "$@"

@rem
@rem Copyright 2015 the original author or authors.
@rem
@rem Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
@rem you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
@rem You may obtain a copy of the License at

@rem distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
@rem WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
@rem See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
@rem limitations under the License.
@rem
@rem SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
@rem

@if "%DEBUG%"=="" @echo off
@rem ##########################################################################
@rem
@rem  Gradle startup script for Windows
@rem
@rem ##########################################################################

@rem Set local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" setlocal

set DIRNAME=%~dp0
if "%DIRNAME%"=="" set DIRNAME=.
@rem This is normally unused
set APP_BASE_NAME=%~n0
set APP_HOME=%DIRNAME%

@rem Resolve any "." and ".." in APP_HOME to make it shorter.
for %%i in ("%APP_HOME%") do set APP_HOME=%%~fi

@rem Add default JVM options here. You can also use JAVA_OPTS and GRADLE_OPTS to pass JVM options to this script.
set DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS="-Xmx64m" "-Xms64m"

@rem Find java.exe
if defined JAVA_HOME goto findJavaFromJavaHome

set JAVA_EXE=java.exe
%JAVA_EXE% -version >NUL 2>&1
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 goto execute

echo. 1>&2
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is not set and no 'java' command could be found in your PATH. 1>&2
echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:findJavaFromJavaHome
set JAVA_HOME=%JAVA_HOME:"=%
set JAVA_EXE=%JAVA_HOME%/bin/java.exe

if exist "%JAVA_EXE%" goto execute

echo. 1>&2
echo ERROR: JAVA_HOME is set to an invalid directory: %JAVA_HOME% 1>&2
echo. 1>&2
echo Please set the JAVA_HOME variable in your environment to match the 1>&2
echo location of your Java installation. 1>&2

goto fail

:execute
@rem Setup the command line

set CLASSPATH=%APP_HOME%\gradle\wrapper\gradle-wrapper.jar


@rem Execute Gradle
"%JAVA_EXE%" %DEFAULT_JVM_OPTS% %JAVA_OPTS% %GRADLE_OPTS% "-Dorg.gradle.appname=%APP_BASE_NAME%" -classpath "%CLASSPATH%" org.gradle.wrapper.GradleWrapperMain %*

:end
@rem End local scope for the variables with windows NT shell
if %ERRORLEVEL% equ 0 goto mainEnd

:fail
rem Set variable GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE if you need the _script_ return code instead of
rem the _cmd.exe /c_ return code!
set EXIT_CODE=%ERRORLEVEL%
if %EXIT_CODE% equ 0 set EXIT_CODE=1
if not ""=="%GRADLE_EXIT_CONSOLE%" exit %EXIT_CODE%
exit /b %EXIT_CODE%

:mainEnd
if "%OS%"=="Windows_NT" endlocal

:omega

## photos/README.txt

````text
ELECTRO Photorealistic Asset Pack

AI-GENERATED photographs are illustrative ONLY, not verified product photos. Individual 512x512 PNG files are divided from 4x4 generated transparent sheets; some items may include edge artifacts or imperfect component geometry. Connector photos extracted from a reference catalog are lower-detail images on white backgrounds.

Technical diagrams are separately drawn and labeled; generic layouts must NOT be used as manufacturer-specific installation wiring. RS485 has no fixed RJ45 pinout. Consult controller technical manuals, applicable standards, and original datasheets before actual wiring.

No 300+ image claim is made: see manifest for actual included files.

````

## scripts/check_comments.py

````python
"""Check KDoc on Kotlin types, functions, member state and constructor properties.

Local functions are included. Temporary local vals and lambda parameters are not
API declarations. Constructor fields accept an adjacent KDoc or @property/@param
on the owning class. Syntax-tree parsing prevents strings and comments from
manufacturing declarations. Install scripts/requirements-dev.txt before running.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import re
import sys
from tree_sitter import Language, Parser
import tree_sitter_kotlin
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
PARSER = Parser(Language(tree_sitter_kotlin.language()))
TYPES = {'class_declaration', 'object_declaration', 'function_declaration', 'secondary_constructor', 'type_alias'}
DENSITY = {'Calculators.kt', 'Engineering.kt', 'App.kt', 'CalculatorScreen.kt', 'AppViewModel.kt'}
def walk(node):
    # Include nested helpers, not just top-level APIs.
    yield node
    for child in node.named_children:
        yield from walk(child)
def preceding_doc(node, source):
    # Annotations belong to the declaration node, so its previous sibling is the KDoc.
    previous = node.prev_named_sibling
    if previous and previous.type == 'block_comment':
        text = source[previous.start_byte:previous.end_byte].decode()
        if text.startswith('/**'):
            return text
    return ''
def declared_name(node, source):
    # Properties wrap their name; annotation names must not be mistaken for property names.
    target = next((n for n in node.named_children if n.type == 'variable_declaration'), node)
    identifiers = [n for n in target.named_children if n.type == 'identifier']
    if not identifiers:
        identifiers = [n for n in walk(target) if n.type == 'identifier']
    return source[identifiers[0].start_byte:identifiers[0].end_byte].decode() if identifiers else node.type

def audit(path):
    # Fail closed on grammar errors rather than reporting incomplete coverage as success.
    source = path.read_bytes()
    tree = PARSER.parse(source)
    failures = []
    if tree.root_node.has_error:
        failures.append(f'{path.relative_to(ROOT)}: Kotlin syntax tree contains an error; coverage is not trustworthy')
    count = 0
    for node in walk(tree.root_node):
        required = node.type in TYPES or (node.type == 'property_declaration' and node.parent.type in {'source_file', 'class_body'})
        if node.type == 'class_parameter' and re.search(rb'\b(val|var)\b', source[node.start_byte:node.end_byte]):
            count += 1
            owner = node.parent.parent.parent
            name = declared_name(node, source)
            if not preceding_doc(node, source) and not re.search(r'@(?:property|param)\s+' + re.escape(name) + r'\b', preceding_doc(owner, source)):
                failures.append(f'{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{node.start_point.row+1}: undocumented constructor property {name}')
        elif required:
            count += 1
            doc = preceding_doc(node, source)
            if not doc:
                failures.append(f'{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{node.start_point.row+1}: undocumented {node.type} {declared_name(node, source)}')
            elif node.type == 'function_declaration':
                parameters = next((n for n in node.named_children if n.type == 'function_value_parameters'), None)
                if parameters:
                    for parameter in parameters.named_children:
                        if parameter.type == 'parameter':
                            name = declared_name(parameter, source)
                            if not re.search(r'@param\s+' + re.escape(name) + r'\b', doc):
                                failures.append(f'{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{node.start_point.row+1}: missing @param {name}')
                if '@return' not in doc:
                    failures.append(f'{path.relative_to(ROOT)}:{node.start_point.row+1}: missing @return contract')
    if path.name in DENSITY:
        comments = sum(source[n.start_byte:n.end_byte].count(b'\n') + 1 for n in walk(tree.root_node) if n.type in {'block_comment', 'line_comment'})
        code = sum(bool(line.strip()) for line in source.decode().splitlines()) - comments
        if comments * 8 < code:
            failures.append(f'{path.name}: {comments} comment lines for {code} code lines; minimum 1:8')
        print(f'{path.name}: {comments} comment lines / {code} nonblank code lines')
    return count, failures

def main():
    # Inspect every shipped source set; generated build output is deliberately outside this tree.
    total, errors = 0, []
    for path in sorted((ROOT / 'app/src').rglob('*.kt')):
        count, failures = audit(path)
        total += count
        errors += failures
    if errors:
        print('\n'.join(errors), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f'PASS: {total} Kotlin declarations documented; five density thresholds met.')
    return 0
if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())

````

## scripts/check_contrast.py

````python
"""Parse shipping theme hex colours, check text contrast, and reject stale evidence.

Use --write only after an intentional palette edit; CI compares committed results.
"""
import argparse
import re
from pathlib import Path
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]

def luminance(rgb):
    # WCAG requires linear-light sRGB, not arithmetic averages of encoded channels.
    channels = [int(rgb[i:i+2],16)/255 for i in (0,2,4)]
    return sum(w*(c/12.92 if c<=.04045 else ((c+.055)/1.055)**2.4) for w,c in zip((.2126,.7152,.0722),channels))

def ratio(fg,bg):
    # Sorting makes the contrast ratio independent of foreground/background order.
    a,b = sorted((luminance(fg),luminance(bg)))
    return (b+.05)/(a+.05)

def token(source,name):
    # Toolbar tokens derive from their actual shared source definitions, not the light palette.
    match = re.search(rf'val {name} = Color\(0xFF([0-9A-Fa-f]{{6}})\)',source)
    assert match, f'Missing colour token {name}'
    return match[1]

def palette(source,name):
    # Missing/changed source syntax fails explicitly instead of retaining an obsolete colour list.
    block = re.search(rf'private val {name}\s*=\s*\w+ColorScheme\((.*?)\n    \)',source,re.S)
    assert block, f'Cannot locate {name} palette'
    values = dict(re.findall(r'(\w+)\s*=\s*Color\(0xFF([0-9A-Fa-f]{6})\)',block[1]))
    if re.search(r'primary\s*=\s*BrandNavy',block[1]):values['primary']=token(source,'BrandNavy')
    return values

def report():
    # All five tested pairs use shipping source tokens; this is not a full-screen accessibility audit.
    source=(ROOT/'app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/ui/theme/Theme.kt').read_text()
    dark,light=palette(source,'Dark'),palette(source,'Light')
    checks=[('dark heading',dark['primary'],dark['background']),('light heading',light['primary'],light['background']),('top bar',token(source,'TopBarText'),token(source,'BrandNavy')),('dark body',dark['onSurface'],dark['background']),('light body',light['onSurface'],light['background'])]
    # Tinted surfaces also carry primary text in cards and chips.
    for name,colors in [('dark',dark),('light',light)]:
        for surface in ['surfaceVariant','surfaceContainer']:
            checks.append((name+' primary on '+surface,colors['primary'],colors[surface]))
        for role in ['primaryContainer','secondaryContainer','tertiaryContainer','errorContainer']:
            checks.append((name+' '+role,colors['on'+role[0].upper()+role[1:]],colors[role]))
    lines=[]
    for name,fg,bg in checks:
        actual=ratio(fg,bg)
        assert actual>=4.5,(name,actual)
        lines.append(f'{name}: {actual:.2f}:1')
    return '\n'.join(lines)+'\n'

def main():
    # Evidence drift fails even if both old and new palettes happen to meet the threshold.
    parser=argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument('--write',action='store_true')
    args=parser.parse_args();result=report();evidence=ROOT/'verification/contrast.txt'
    if args.write:evidence.write_text(result)
    else:assert evidence.read_text()==result,'Stale contrast evidence; run scripts/check_contrast.py --write'
    print(result,end='')
if __name__=='__main__':main()

````

## scripts/check_reference_links.py

````python
"""Optional online URL reachability audit; never called by the offline application.

An HTTP response is not proof that a page supports a table. Sites may reject
HEAD requests or automated clients. This script records that distinction.
"""
import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
from pathlib import Path
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
parser=argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--output',default=str(root/'verification/reference-links.json'))
args=parser.parse_args()
a=root/'app/src/main/assets'
pages=json.loads((a/'pages.json').read_text())
modules=json.loads((a/'modules.json').read_text())
urls=sorted({url for page in pages.values() for url in page['sources']} | {p['source'] for parts in modules.values() for p in parts} | {v for parts in modules.values() for p in parts for v in p['specs'].values() if v.startswith('https://')})
def check(url):
    # A blocked HEAD response is inconclusive; reachability never certifies table accuracy.
    try:
        request=urllib.request.Request(url,method='HEAD',headers={'User-Agent':'ElectroKit-reference-check/1.0'})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(request,timeout=15) as r:return {'url':url,'status':r.status,'resolved_url':r.url,'checked':'reachability only'}
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:return {'url':url,'status':e.code,'checked':'blocked, unavailable, or HEAD unsupported; manual check needed'}
    except Exception as e:return {'url':url,'error':type(e).__name__,'checked':'could not verify'}
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=12) as pool:results=list(pool.map(check,urls))
Path(args.output).write_text(json.dumps(results,indent=2)+'\n')
print(f'{len(results)} reference URLs checked for reachability; see output for limitations.')

````

## scripts/package_project.py

````python
"""Generate the complete source listing/tree/checksums, or check them in CI.

Usage: python scripts/package_project.py [--check]
The delivered ZIP is assembled separately so signing credentials never enter
this project. Source and verification files, including this generator, are
covered by the resulting checksums.
"""
import argparse
import base64
import hashlib
from pathlib import Path

root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
parser=argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--check',action='store_true')
args=parser.parse_args()
generated={'FULL_SOURCE.md','PROJECT_TREE.txt','SHA256SUMS.txt'}
def files():
    # Exclude private signing material and machine state from the public source listing.
    return sorted(p for p in root.rglob('*') if p.is_file() and
        not set(p.relative_to(root).parts)&{'.git','.venv','venv','build','build-before-audit','.gradle','.idea','.kotlin','__pycache__'} and
        p.name!='local.properties' and p.suffix not in {'.apk','.aab','.jks','.keystore','.pyc'})
def checksum(path):
    # Hash exact bytes so unrecorded source or line-ending changes fail the packaging gate.
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
if args.check:
    lines=(root/'SHA256SUMS.txt').read_text().splitlines()
    known={name:digest for digest,name in (line.split('  ',1) for line in lines)}
    actual={str(p.relative_to(root)):checksum(p) for p in files() if p.name!='SHA256SUMS.txt'}
    assert known==actual,'Source files/listings/checksums changed; run scripts/package_project.py again.'
    print('PASS: complete source/listing checksums match.')
else:
    source=[p for p in files() if p.name not in generated]
    names=sorted([str(p.relative_to(root)) for p in source]+list(generated))
    (root/'PROJECT_TREE.txt').write_text('Electro/\n'+''.join('  '+n+'\n' for n in names))
    listing=['# Electro — complete project source\n\nGenerated by scripts/package_project.py. Edit source files, then regenerate.\n\n']
    for p in source:
        name=str(p.relative_to(root))
        if p.suffix.lower() in {'.png','.webp','.jpg','.jpeg'}:
            listing.append(f'## {name}\n\nBinary image asset; see this path and SHA256SUMS.txt for its exact bytes/hash.\n\n')
            continue
        try:
            content=p.read_text()
            language={'.kt':'kotlin','.kts':'kotlin','.xml':'xml','.json':'json','.py':'python','.yml':'yaml','.md':'markdown'}.get(p.suffix,'text')
        except UnicodeDecodeError:
            content=base64.b64encode(p.read_bytes()).decode()+'\n'
            language='text'
            name+=' (Base64)'
        fence='`'*max(4,max((len(x) for x in __import__('re').findall('`+',content)),default=0)+1)
        listing.append(f'## {name}\n\n{fence}{language}\n{content}\n{fence}\n\n')
    (root/'FULL_SOURCE.md').write_text(''.join(listing))
    (root/'SHA256SUMS.txt').write_text(''.join(checksum(p)+'  '+str(p.relative_to(root))+'\n' for p in files() if p.name!='SHA256SUMS.txt'))
    print(f'Generated listing, tree and checksums for {len(names)} files.')

````

## scripts/test_quality_checks.py

````python
"""Regression checks for documentation coverage and source-derived palette evidence."""
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch
import check_comments
import check_contrast

class QualityGateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Prove that the gates depend on source content, including negative fixtures."""
    def test_undocumented_function_is_rejected(self):
        # Declaration-shaped text inside strings cannot document or hide a real function.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=check_comments.ROOT) as directory:
            path=Path(directory)/'Fixture.kt'
            path.write_text('val ignored = "fun fake() {}"\nfun missing() {}\n')
            count,failures=check_comments.audit(path)
            self.assertGreaterEqual(count,2)
            self.assertTrue(any('function_declaration missing' in f for f in failures))
    def test_annotated_function_and_constructor_property_docs_pass(self):
        # Annotations belong to the declaration; constructor fields can use class @property docs.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=check_comments.ROOT) as directory:
            path=Path(directory)/'Fixture.kt'
            path.write_text('/** Owner. @property value Stored scalar. */\nclass Owner(val value: Int) {\n/** Mutation. @return Unit; no errors. */\n@Deprecated("fixture")\nfun mutate() {}\n}\n')
            count,failures=check_comments.audit(path)
            self.assertEqual(3,count)
            self.assertEqual([],failures)
    def test_source_token_changes_change_contrast_report(self):
        # A hard-coded duplicate colour list would incorrectly leave the report unchanged.
        source=(check_contrast.ROOT/'app/src/main/java/com/electrokit/app/ui/theme/Theme.kt').read_text()
        original=check_contrast.report()
        with patch.object(Path,'read_text',return_value=source.replace('0xFF93B4FF','0xFFFFFFFF')):
            self.assertNotEqual(original,check_contrast.report())
    def test_committed_contrast_evidence_is_current(self):
        # Stale numbers are rejected even if old and new palettes both pass 4.5:1.
        self.assertEqual((check_contrast.ROOT/'verification/contrast.txt').read_text(),check_contrast.report())
if __name__=='__main__':unittest.main()

````

"""Validate offline registry, links, table shapes and module coverage using Python 3."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from collections import Counter
# Validate shape and offline coverage, not electrical accuracy or standards compliance.
root=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
a=root/'app/src/main/assets'
registry=json.loads((a/'registry.json').read_text())
pages=json.loads((a/'pages.json').read_text())
modules=json.loads((a/'modules.json').read_text())
assert Counter(x['tab'] for x in registry)=={'CALCULATORS':31,'PIN-OUTS':55,'RESOURCES':21,'PLUGINS':3}
assert len({x['id'] for x in registry})==len(registry)
assert len({x['icon'] for x in registry})==len(registry)
for entry in registry:
    if entry['screenType']=='reference':assert entry['contentId'] in pages,entry
    if entry['screenType']=='module':assert len(modules[entry['id']])>=30
used={e['contentId'] for e in registry if e['screenType']=='reference'}
assert set(pages)==used, ('Unreferenced or missing pages',set(pages)^used)
for key,page in pages.items():
    assert page['title'] and page['sections'],key
    for s in page['sections']:
        assert s['title'] and s['headers'] and s['rows'],(key,s)
        for i,header in enumerate(s['headers']):
            assert any(row[i].strip() for row in s['rows']),(key,s['title'],'Empty column',header)
        for row in s['rows']:assert len(row)==len(s['headers']),(key,s['title'],row,s['headers'])
        for d in s['diagrams']:
            assert d['caption']
            for pin in d['pins']:assert pin['label'] and 0<=pin['x']<=1 and 0<=pin['y']<=1,(key,pin)
for key,entries in modules.items():
    assert len({p['name'] for p in entries})==len(entries)
    assert all(p['name'] and p['category'] and p['specs'] and p['source'].startswith('https://') for p in entries)
    for part in entries:
        assert set(part['numericKeys'])<=set(part['specs']),(key,part['name'])
        assert not {'Description','Use','Package note'} & set(part['numericKeys'])
        for name in part['numericKeys']:
            value=part['specs'][name].replace('−','-')
            try: float(value)
            except ValueError: raise AssertionError((part['name'],name,value))
manifest=(root/'app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml').read_text()
assert 'INTERNET' not in manifest and 'uses-permission' not in manifest

# Every page must disclose provenance; URL presence alone must not imply verified table cells.
assert all(p.get("provenance", "").strip() for p in pages.values())

print('PASS: 31 calculators, 55 pin-outs, 21 resources, 3 modules; all routes, tables, diagrams and module records are structurally valid.')

## scripts/validate_engineering.py

````python
"""Validate the exact supplied fault import and the complete offline engineering reference graph.

Uses only Python's standard library; no Android SDK, network access or pytest is required.
This checks source integrity and navigation, not OEM approval or handwritten electrical accuracy.
"""
import json
from pathlib import Path


def main():
    # Compare immutable original fields separately from derived explanations and navigational indexes.
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    data = json.loads((root / 'app/src/main/assets/engineering.json').read_text())
    tools = json.loads((root / 'app/src/main/assets/engineering_tools.json').read_text())
    rows = (root / 'app/src/test/resources/faults-original.tsv').read_text().splitlines()
    actual = ['|'.join(map(str, [f['serial'], f['code'], f['message'], f['reset'], f['group']])) for f in data['faults']]
    assert rows == actual and len(rows) == 125
    assert {f['serial'] for f in data['faults']} == set(range(1, 129)) - {112, 113, 114}
    assert len({f['code'] for f in data['faults']}) == 125
    ids = {r['id'] for r in data['records']}
    sources = {s['id'] for s in data['sources']}
    assert len(ids) == len(data['records'])
    assert sum(s['type'] == 'Photograph transcription' for s in data['sources']) == 14
    for record in data['records'] + data['faults']:
        assert record['sources'] and set(record['sources']) <= sources
        assert set(record['related']) <= ids
    for marker in data['markers']:
        assert marker['record'] in ids and marker['source'] in sources
        assert 0 <= marker['x'] <= 1000 and 0 <= marker['y'] <= 560
    assert len({t['id'] for t in tools}) == len(tools) == 15
    for tool in tools:
        assert tool['formula'] and tool['assumptions'] and tool['fields']
        assert len({f['key'] for f in tool['fields']}) == len(tool['fields'])
    assert 'output-Q9–Q12' in ids
    assert not {'output-Q9', 'output-Q10', 'output-Q11', 'output-Q12'} & ids
    print(f"PASS: 125 exact faults, {len(ids)} technical records, 14 photographs, 15 tools; all sources and routes resolve.")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

````

## scripts/validate_library.py

````python
"""Validate bundled component IDs, protected grouping, PNG integrity and image-memory boundaries."""
import hashlib
import json
import struct
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'app/src/main/assets'


def validate(root=ROOT):
    """Reject broken links/traversal, duplicate records/images and corrupt image headers."""
    records = json.loads((root / 'components.json').read_text())
    ids, images, hashes = set(), set(), set()
    for item in records:
        assert all(isinstance(item.get(k), str) and item[k] for k in ('id', 'name', 'category', 'image')), item
        assert item['id'] not in ids, f"Duplicate component ID: {item['id']}"
        ids.add(item['id'])
        path = (root / item['image']).resolve()
        assert path.is_relative_to(root.resolve() / 'components'), f"Image outside component directory: {item['image']}"
        data = path.read_bytes()
        assert data[:8] == b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n', path
        width, height = struct.unpack('>II', data[16:24])
        assert 0 < width <= 4096 and 0 < height <= 4096, (path, width, height)
        if path not in images:
            digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
            assert digest not in hashes, f'Duplicate image bytes: {path}; reuse the same asset path'
            hashes.add(digest)
        images.add(path)
    actual = {p.resolve() for p in (root / 'components').glob('*.png')}
    assert actual == images, 'Unreferenced or missing component files'
    assert any(item['category'] == 'Escalator' for item in records), 'Protected category missing'
    assert sum(p.stat().st_size for p in images) < 32 * 1024 * 1024, 'Review excessive library size'
    print(f"PASS: {len(records)} component records, {len(images)} unique PNGs, explicit Escalator category, valid local paths and dimensions.")


if __name__ == '__main__':
    validate()

````

<div class="metadata"><div class="explanation" id="explanationUnusedAttribute" style="display: none;">
This check finds attributes set in XML files that were introduced in a version newer than the oldest version targeted by your application (with the <code>minSdkVersion</code> attribute).<br/>
<br/>
This is not an error; the application will simply ignore the attribute. However, if the attribute is important to the appearance or functionality of your application, you should consider finding an alternative way to achieve the same result with only available attributes, and then you can optionally create a copy of the layout in a layout-vNN folder which will be used on API NN or higher where you can take advantage of the newer attribute.<br/>
<br/>
Note: This check does not only apply to attributes. For example, some tags can be unused too, such as the new <code>&lt;tag></code> element in layouts introduced in API 21.<br/>Note: This issue has an associated quickfix operation in Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA.<br>
To suppress this error, use the issue id "UnusedAttribute" as explained in the <a href="#SuppressInfo">Suppressing Warnings and Errors</a> section.<br/>
<br/></div>

<div class="metadata"><div class="explanation" id="explanationGradleDependency" style="display: none;">
This detector looks for usages of libraries where the version you are using is not the current stable release. Using older versions is fine, and there are cases where you deliberately want to stick with an older version. However, you may simply not be aware that a more recent version is available, and that is what this lint check helps find.<br/>Note: This issue has an associated quickfix operation in Android Studio and IntelliJ IDEA.<br>
To suppress this error, use the issue id "GradleDependency" as explained in the <a href="#SuppressInfo">Suppressing Warnings and Errors</a> section.<br/>
<br/></div>

              <div class="mdl-card__supporting-text">
This card lists all the extra checks run by lint, provided from libraries,
